title.zh: 卷九十八 列傳第三十六: 完顏匡 完顏綱弟:定奴
title.en: Volume 98 Biographies 36: Wan Yankuang, Wan Yangang younger brother: Dingnu
title.raw: 卷九十八 列傳第三十六: 完顏匡 完顏綱弟:定奴 Volume 98 Biographies 36: Wan Yankuang, Wan Yangang younger brother: Dingnu

sentences.zh: 完顏匡

translations.literal: Wan Yan Kuang
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Kuang

sentences.zh: 完顏匡，本名撒速，始祖九世孫。

translations.literal: Wan Yan Kuang, original name Sasu, was a ninth-generation descendant of the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Kuang, whose original name was Sasu, was a ninth-generation descendant of the dynastic founder.

sentences.zh: 事豳王允成，為其府教讀。

translations.literal: He served Prince Bin Yongcheng as tutor-reader in his princely household.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the service of Prince Bin Yongcheng and served as tutor-reader in his household.

sentences.zh: 大定十九年，章宗年十餘歲，顯宗命詹事烏林答願擇德行淳謹、才學該通者，使教章宗兄弟。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Dading, Zhangzong was a little more than ten years old; Xianzong ordered the Household Mentor Wanyan Yuan to select men of pure and careful conduct and comprehensive learning to teach Zhangzong and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Dading (1179), Zhangzong was in his early teens. Xianzong ordered the Household Mentor Wanyan Yuan to choose men of upright, careful character and broad learning to instruct Zhangzong and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 閱月，願啟顯宗曰：「豳王府教讀完顏撒速、徐王府教讀僕散訛可二人，可使教皇孫兄弟。」

translations.literal: After a month Yuan reported to Xianzong, saying, "The Bin princely household tutor-reader Wan Yan Sasu and the Xu princely household tutor-reader Pusan Yuke—these two men may be employed to teach the emperor's grandsons and their brothers."
translations.idiomatic: A month later Yuan reported to Xianzong: "Wanyan Sasu, tutor-reader in the Bin princely household, and Pusan Yuke, tutor-reader in the Xu princely household—these two are fit to instruct the imperial grandsons and their brothers."

sentences.zh: 顯宗曰：「典教幼子，須用淳謹者。」

translations.literal: Xianzong said, "In instructing young children one must employ men who are pure and careful."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong said, "To teach young boys properly, one must use men who are steady and conscientious."

sentences.zh: 已而召見于承華殿西便殿。

translations.literal: Thereafter they were summoned for audience in the western side hall of the Chenghua Palace.
translations.idiomatic: They were then summoned to audience in the western side chamber of the Chenghua Palace.

sentences.zh: 顯宗問其年，對曰：「臣生之歲，海陵自上京遷中都，歲在壬申。」

translations.literal: Xianzong asked his age; he replied, "The year of my birth was when Hailing moved the capital from Shangjing to Zhongdu—the year renshen."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong asked his age. He answered, "I was born in the year when Emperor Hailing moved the capital from Shangjing to Zhongdu—the renshen year."

sentences.zh: 顯宗曰：「二十八歲爾，詹事乃雲三十歲何也？」

translations.literal: Xianzong said, "You are twenty-eight years old; why did the Household Mentor say thirty?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong said, "You are twenty-eight—why did the Household Mentor say thirty?"

sentences.zh: 匡曰：「臣年止如此，詹事謂臣出入宮禁，故增其歲言之耳。」

translations.literal: Kuang said, "My years are only so many; the Household Mentor, because I enter and leave the palace precincts, therefore added to my years in speaking of me."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang said, "My age is no more than that. The Household Mentor thought that because I move in and out of the palace precincts, he should speak of me as somewhat older."

sentences.zh: 顯宗顧謂近臣曰：「篤實人也。」

translations.literal: Xianzong turned and said to those near him, "A sincere and solid man."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong turned to those beside him and said, "A man of genuine integrity."

sentences.zh: 命擇日，使皇孫行師弟子禮。

translations.literal: He ordered a day to be chosen for the imperial grandsons to perform the rites of master and pupil.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a day chosen for the imperial grandsons to perform the ceremony of master and pupil.

sentences.zh: 七月丁亥，宣宗、章宗皆就學，顯宗曰：「每日先教漢字，至申時漢字課畢，教女直小字，習國朝語。」

translations.literal: On the dinghai day of the seventh month Xuanzong and Zhangzong both began their studies; Xianzong said, "Each day teach Chinese characters first; when the Chinese lesson is finished at the hour shen, teach the Jurchen small script and practice the national language."
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the seventh month, Xuanzong and Zhangzong both began their lessons. Xianzong said, "Each day teach Chinese characters first; when the Chinese lesson ends at the hour of shen, teach the Jurchen small script and practice the national tongue."

sentences.zh: 因賜酒及彩幣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed wine and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: He then rewarded them with wine and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 頃之，世宗詔匡、訛可俱充太子侍讀。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Shizong decreed that Kuang and Yuke should both serve as tutors to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shizong appointed Kuang and Yuke both as tutors to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 寢殿小底駝滿九住問匡曰：「伯夷、叔齊何如人？」

translations.literal: The sleeping-hall attendant Tuoman Jiuzhu asked Kuang, "What sort of men were Boyi and Shuqi?"
translations.idiomatic: Tuoman Jiuzhu, an attendant of the sleeping hall, asked Kuang, "What sort of men were Boyi and Shuqi?"

sentences.zh: 匡曰：「孔子稱夷、齊求仁得仁。」

translations.literal: Kuang said, "Confucius praised Yi and Qi as having sought benevolence and obtained it."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang said, "Confucius praised Boyi and Shuqi for seeking benevolence and attaining it."

sentences.zh: 九住曰：「汝輩學古，惟前言是信。

translations.literal: Jiuzhu said, "You people who study antiquity believe only what the ancients said.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhu said, "You scholars of antiquity believe only what the ancients said.

sentences.zh: 夷、齊輕去其親，不食周粟餓死首陽山，仁者固如是乎？」

translations.literal: Yi and Qi lightly abandoned their kin, refused to eat Zhou grain, and starved to death on Mount Shouyang—is this how benevolent men are supposed to be?"
translations.idiomatic: Boyi and Shuqi lightly abandoned their kin, refused Zhou grain, and starved to death on Mount Shouyang—is that what a benevolent man does?"

sentences.zh: 匡曰：「不然，古之賢者行其義也，行其道也。

translations.literal: Kuang said, "Not so—the sages of antiquity acted according to righteousness and walked the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang said, "Not at all. The sages of antiquity acted according to righteousness and followed the Way.

sentences.zh: 伯夷思成其父之志以去其國，叔齊不苟從父之志亦去其國。

translations.literal: Boyi, wishing to fulfill his father's intent, left the state; Shuqi, unwilling to follow his father's intent in a perfunctory way, also left the state.
translations.idiomatic: Boyi wished to fulfill his father's intent and therefore left the state; Shuqi, unwilling to follow his father's intent merely for form's sake, left the state as well.

sentences.zh: 武王伐紂，夷、齊叩馬而諫。

translations.literal: When King Wu attacked Zhou, Yi and Qi seized the horse's bridle and remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu marched against King Zhou, Boyi and Shuqi seized the bridle of his horse and remonstrated with him.

sentences.zh: 紂死，殷為周，夷、齊不食周粟，遂餓而死。

translations.literal: When Zhou died and Yin became Zhou, Yi and Qi would not eat Zhou grain and thus starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou fell and Yin became Zhou, Boyi and Shuqi refused Zhou grain and starved to death.

sentences.zh: 正君臣之分，為天下後世慮至遠也，非仁人而能若是乎！」

translations.literal: They rectified the distinction between ruler and minister and looked far ahead for the world and for posterity—could anyone but a benevolent man have done thus!"
translations.idiomatic: They upheld the distinction between ruler and subject and looked far ahead for the realm and for generations to come—could anyone but a man of benevolence have acted thus?"

sentences.zh: 是時，世宗如春水，顯宗從，二人者馬上相語遂後。

translations.literal: At that time Shizong was at Chunshui and Xianzong accompanied him; the two men conversed on horseback and fell behind.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shizong was at Chunshui and Xianzong accompanied him; the two men talked on horseback and fell behind the procession.

sentences.zh: 顯宗遲九住至，問曰：「何以後也？」

translations.literal: Xianzong waited for Jiuzhu to arrive and asked, "Why are you behind?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong waited for Jiuzhu to catch up and asked, "Why have you fallen behind?"

sentences.zh: 九住以對，顯宗歎曰：「不以女直文字譯經史，何以知此。

translations.literal: Jiuzhu answered; Xianzong sighed and said, "Had the classics and histories not been translated into Jurchen script, how could one know this?
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhu gave his answer. Xianzong sighed and said, "Without translating the classics and histories into Jurchen script, how could one know such things?

sentences.zh: 主上立女直科舉，教以經史，乃能得其淵奧如此哉。」

translations.literal: When the sovereign established Jurchen examinations and taught the classics and histories, only then could one attain such profundity as this!"
translations.idiomatic: When His Majesty established the Jurchen examinations and taught the classics and histories, men could reach such depth of understanding!"

sentences.zh: 稱善者良久，謂九住曰：「《論語》'知之為知之，不知為不知，是知也'。

translations.literal: He praised this at length, then said to Jiuzhu, "The Analects says, 'To know what you know and know what you do not know—this is knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: He praised this at length, then told Jiuzhu, "The Analects says: 'To know when you know and to know when you do not know—this is knowledge.

sentences.zh: 汝不知不達，務辯口以難人。

translations.literal: You do not know and do not understand, yet you strive with glib speech to make things difficult for others.
translations.idiomatic: You neither know nor understand, yet you use clever talk to make things hard for others.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，人之學、不學，豈不相遠哉。」

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, are those who study and those who do not study not far apart indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, how far apart are those who study and those who do not!"

sentences.zh: 顯宗嘗謂中侍局都監蒲察查刺曰：「入殿小底完顏訛出、侍讀完顏撒速，與我同族，汝知之乎？」

translations.literal: Xianzong once said to the chief superintendent of the Central Attendants Bureau, Pucha Zhaci, "The palace attendant Wan Yan Echu and the tutor Wan Yan Sasu are of my clan—do you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong once told Pucha Zhaci, chief superintendent of the Central Attendants Bureau: "The palace attendant Wanyan Echu and the tutor Wanyan Sasu are of my clan. Did you know that?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不知也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "I did not know."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I did not know."

sentences.zh: 顯宗曰：「撒速，始祖九世孫。

translations.literal: Xianzong said, "Sasu is a ninth-generation descendant of the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong said, "Sasu is a ninth-generation descendant of the founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 訛出，保活裏之世也。

translations.literal: Echu belongs to the generation of Baohuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Echu belongs to the generation of Baohuoli.

sentences.zh: 始祖兄弟皆非常人，汝何由知此。」

translations.literal: The founding ancestor's brothers were all extraordinary men—how could you have known this?"
translations.idiomatic: The founder's brothers were all extraordinary men—how could you have known that?"

sentences.zh: 顯宗命匡作《睿宗功德歌》，教章宗歌之，其詞曰：「我祖睿宗，厚有陰德。

translations.literal: Xianzong ordered Kuang to compose the "Song of the Merits and Virtues of Emperor Ruizong" and taught Zhangzong to sing it; its words run: "My ancestor Emperor Ruizong possessed deep hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong ordered Kuang to compose the "Song of the Merits and Virtues of Emperor Ruizong" and taught Zhangzong to sing it. The text begins: "My ancestor Emperor Ruizong possessed deep hidden virtue.

sentences.zh: 國祚有傳，儲嗣當立。

translations.literal: The dynastic fortune had a successor; the heir apparent ought to be established.
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic fortune had a line of succession; the heir ought to be established.

sentences.zh: 滿朝疑懼，獨先啟策。

translations.literal: The whole court was doubtful and afraid; he alone first opened the plan.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court was filled with doubt and fear; he alone first set forth the plan.

sentences.zh: 徂征三秦，震驚來附。

translations.literal: He marched to conquer the Three Qins; in awe they came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against the Three Qin; awed, they came to submit.

sentences.zh: 富平百萬，望風奔僕。

translations.literal: At Fuping a million men fled before the wind like servants.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuping a million men scattered before the wind like servants in flight.

sentences.zh: 靈恩光被，時雨春暘。

translations.literal: Spiritual favor spread abroad like light; timely rain and spring sunshine.
translations.idiomatic: His spiritual grace spread abroad; timely rain and spring sunshine followed.

sentences.zh: 神化周浹，春生冬藏。」

translations.literal: His transforming influence pervaded all; spring gave birth and winter stored away."
translations.idiomatic: His transforming power reached everywhere; spring brought life and winter stored it away."

sentences.zh: 蓋取宗翰與睿宗定策立熙宗，及平陝西大破張浚于富平也。

translations.literal: This alludes to Zonghan and Emperor Ruizong deciding the policy to establish Emperor Xizong, and to pacifying Shaanxi and crushing Zhang Jun at Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: The song alludes to Zonghan and Emperor Ruizong deciding the policy that established Emperor Xizong, and to the pacification of Shaanxi and the great defeat of Zhang Jun at Fuping.

sentences.zh: 二十三年三月萬春節，顯宗命章宗歌此詞侑觴，世宗愕然曰：「汝輩何因知此？」

translations.literal: On the Wanchun festival of the third month of the twenty-third year Xianzong ordered Zhangzong to sing these words to accompany the cups; Shizong was startled and said, "How do you people know this?"
translations.idiomatic: At the Wanchun festival in the third month of the twenty-third year, Xianzong had Zhangzong sing these lines to accompany the toasts. Shizong was astonished and said, "How do you know this?"

sentences.zh: 顯宗奏曰：「臣伏讀《睿宗皇帝實錄》，欲使兒子知創業之艱難，命侍讀撒速作歌教之。」

translations.literal: Xianzong reported, "Your servant has read the Veritable Records of Emperor Ruizong and wished to let my son know the hardships of founding the enterprise; I ordered the tutor Sasu to compose a song to teach him."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong reported, "I have studied the Veritable Records of Emperor Ruizong and wished my son to understand the hardships of founding the dynasty. I ordered the tutor Sasu to compose a song and teach it to him."

sentences.zh: 世宗大喜，顧謂諸王侍臣曰：「朕念睿宗皇帝功德，恐子孫無由知，皇太子能追念作歌以教其子，嘉哉盛事，朕之樂豈有量哉。

translations.literal: Shizong was greatly pleased and, turning to the princes and attendants, said, "I think of Emperor Ruizong's merits and virtues and fear that posterity may have no means to know them; the crown prince can commemorate them by composing a song to teach his son—what a fine and splendid affair! My joy cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was greatly pleased and said to the princes and attendants, "I cherish Emperor Ruizong's merits and virtues and fear that posterity may never learn of them. The crown prince can commemorate them by composing a song to teach his son—what a splendid thing! My joy knows no measure.

sentences.zh: 卿等亦當誦習，以不忘祖宗之功。」

translations.literal: You too should recite and study it, so as not to forget the achievements of the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: You too should learn and recite it, so as not to forget the achievements of our forebears."

sentences.zh: 命章宗歌數四，酒行極歡，乙夜乃罷。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhangzong to sing it several times; the wine passed in the utmost joy, and only at the second watch did it end.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhangzong sing it several times. The banquet reached its height of joy and did not end until the second watch of the night.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，匡中禮部策論進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Kuang passed the Ministry of Rites policy-essay examination for presented scholar.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Kuang passed the Ministry of Rites policy-essay examination and became a presented scholar.

sentences.zh: 是歲，世宗在上京，顯宗監國。

translations.literal: That year Shizong was at Shangjing and Xianzong supervised the state.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shizong was at Shangjing while Xianzong supervised affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰，禦試，前一日癸卯，讀卷官吏部侍郎李晏、棣州防禦使把內刺、國史院編修官夾谷衡、國子助教尼龐古 鑒進稟，策題問「契敷五教，皋陶明五刑，是以刑措不用，比屋可封。

translations.literal: On the jiachen day of the third month was the imperial examination; on the preceding guimao day the examiners—the Vice Minister of Personnel Li Yan, the Defender of Dizhou Baneici, the Historiography Compiler Jiagu Heng, and the National University Assistant Instructor Nipanggu Jian—submitted their report; the policy topic asked, "Qi spread the Five Teachings and Gao Yao clarified the Five Punishments, so punishments were set aside unused and every household could be sealed in praise.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the third month came the imperial examination. On the preceding guimao day the examiners—Vice Minister of Personnel Li Yan, Defender of Dizhou Baneici, Historiography Compiler Jiagu Heng, and National University Assistant Instructor Nipanggu Jian—submitted their report. The policy question asked: "Qi spread the Five Teachings and Gao Yao clarified the Five Punishments, so that punishments fell into disuse and every household could be sealed in praise.

sentences.zh: 今欲興教化，措刑罰，振紀綱，施之萬世，何術可致？」

translations.literal: Now we wish to revive instruction and transformation, set punishments aside, strengthen discipline and statutes, and extend this for ten thousand generations—by what method can this be achieved?"
translations.idiomatic: Now we wish to revive instruction and transformation, set punishments aside, strengthen discipline and statutes, and extend this for ten thousand generations—by what means can this be achieved?"

sentences.zh: 匡已試，明日入見，顯宗問對策雲何，匡曰：「臣熟觀策問敷教、措刑兩事，不詳'振紀綱'一句，只作兩事對，策必不能中。」

translations.literal: Kuang had already taken the examination; the next day he was received in audience; Xianzong asked how his policy answer had been; Kuang said, "Your servant closely examined the policy question on spreading instruction and setting punishments aside but did not treat in detail the phrase 'strengthen discipline and statutes'; if one answers only on two matters, the policy answer certainly cannot pass."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang had already taken the examination. The next day he was received in audience. Xianzong asked how his policy answer had gone. Kuang said, "I studied the question closely. It treats spreading instruction and setting punishments aside, but I did not address the phrase 'strengthen discipline and statutes' in full. If one answers only on two points, the essay certainly cannot pass."

sentences.zh: 顯宗命匡誦所對策，終篇，曰：「是亦當中。」

translations.literal: Xianzong ordered Kuang to recite his policy answer through to the end and said, "This too ought to pass."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong had Kuang recite his answer from beginning to end and said, "This ought to pass as well."

sentences.zh: 匡曰：「編修衡、助教鑒長於選校，必不能中。」

translations.literal: Kuang said, "Compiler Heng and Assistant Instructor Jian excel at collation; they certainly cannot pass."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang said, "Compiler Heng and Assistant Instructor Jian excel at collation—they certainly cannot pass."

sentences.zh: 已而匡果下第。

translations.literal: Thereafter Kuang indeed failed the examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Kuang failed the examination as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 顯宗惜之，謂侍臣曰：「我只欲問教化、刑罰兩事，乃添振紀綱一句，命刪去，李晏固執不可，今果誤人矣。」

translations.literal: Xianzong regretted it and said to the attendants, "I only wished to ask about instruction and transformation and about punishments, yet the phrase on strengthening discipline and statutes was added; I ordered it deleted, but Li Yan obstinately would not agree—now it has indeed misled people."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong regretted the outcome and told his attendants, "I only wanted to ask about instruction and transformation and about punishments, yet someone added the phrase on strengthening discipline and statutes. I ordered it removed, but Li Yan stubbornly refused—and now it has indeed misled the candidates."

sentences.zh: 謂侍正石敦寺家奴、唐括曷答曰：「侍讀二十一年府試不中，我本不欲侍讀再試，恐傷其志，今乃下第，使人意不樂。」

translations.literal: He said to the attendant-in-chief Shi Dunsi Jianu and Tangguo Hedada, "The tutor failed the princely household examination in the twenty-first year; I originally did not wish him to take the examination again, fearing to wound his resolve—now he has failed after all, which makes one's heart uneasy."
translations.idiomatic: He said to the attendant-in-chief Shi Dunsi Jianu and Tangguo Hedada, "The tutor failed the princely household examination in the twenty-first year. I did not want him to sit the examination again for fear of wounding his spirit—and now he has failed after all. It is disheartening."

sentences.zh: 是歲初取止四十五人，顯宗命添五人，僕散訛可中在四十五人，後除書畫直長。

translations.literal: That year only forty-five men were initially selected; Xianzong ordered five more to be added; Pusan Yuke passed among the forty-five and was later appointed director of calligraphy and painting.
translations.idiomatic: That year only forty-five candidates were initially selected. Xianzong ordered five more added. Pusan Yuke passed among the forty-five and was later appointed director of calligraphy and painting.

sentences.zh: 匡與訛可俱為侍讀，匡被眷遇特異，顯宗謂匡曰：「汝無以訛可登第怏怏，但善教金源郡王，何官不可至哉。」

translations.literal: Kuang and Yuke were both tutors; Kuang received exceptional favor; Xianzong said to Kuang, "Do not be resentful because Yuke passed the examination—only teach the Prince of Jinyuan well, and what office may you not reach?"
translations.idiomatic: Kuang and Yuke remained tutors together, but Kuang enjoyed exceptional favor. Xianzong told him, "Do not brood because Yuke passed the examination. Teach the Prince of Jinyuan well, and what office may you not attain?"

sentences.zh: 是歲，顯宗薨，章宗判大興尹，封原王，拜右丞相，立為皇太孫。

translations.literal: That year Xianzong died; Zhangzong served as administrator of Daxing, was enfeoffed as Prince Yuan, appointed Right Chancellor, and established as imperial great-grandson heir.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xianzong died. Zhangzong was made administrator of Daxing, enfeoffed as Prince Yuan, appointed Right Chancellor, and established as imperial great-grandson heir.

sentences.zh: 匡仍為太孫侍讀。

translations.literal: Kuang remained tutor to the great-grandson heir.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang continued as tutor to the great-grandson heir.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，匡試詩賦，漏寫詩題下注字，不取，特賜及第，除中都路教授，侍讀如故。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year Kuang took the poetry-and-rhapsody examination, omitted the subscript characters under the poem title, and was not selected; he was specially granted passage, appointed professor on the Zhongdu circuit, and remained tutor as before."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year Kuang took the poetry-and-rhapsody examination but omitted the subscript characters under the poem title and was not selected. He was specially granted passage, appointed professor on the Zhongdu circuit, and retained his post as tutor."

sentences.zh: 章宗立提刑司，專糾察黜陟，當時號為外台，匡與司空襄，參政揆奏：「息民不如省官，聖朝舊無提刑司，皇統、大定間每數歲一遣使廉察，郡縣稱治。

translations.literal: Zhangzong established the Office for Punishing Crime, devoted exclusively to investigation and promotion or demotion; at the time it was called the Outer Court; Kuang together with Sikong Xiang and Participating Minister Kui memorialized, "To give the people rest is not as good as reducing officials; the holy dynasty formerly had no Office for Punishing Crime; during Huangtong and Dading an envoy for honest investigation was sent every few years and the commanderies and counties were said to be well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong established the Office for Punishing Crime, devoted solely to investigation and promotion or demotion; at the time it was called the Outer Court. Kuang, together with Sikong Xiang and Participating Minister Kui, memorialized: "Giving the people rest is better achieved by reducing officials. The holy dynasty formerly had no such office; during Huangtong and Dading an honest-investigation envoy was sent every few years, and the commanderies and counties were well governed.

sentences.zh: 自立此官，冀達下情，今乃是非混淆，徒煩聖聽。

translations.literal: Since this office was established, it was hoped to reach the sentiments below; now right and wrong are confused and the holy ear is troubled in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Since this office was established, it was meant to reach the sentiments of the people below, yet now right and wrong are confused and the sovereign's attention is troubled in vain.

sentences.zh: 自古無提點刑獄專薦舉之權者，若陛下不欲遽更，不宜使兼採訪廉能之任。

translations.literal: From antiquity there has never been one who held the post of supervising punishments with exclusive authority to recommend and promote; if Your Majesty does not wish to change it immediately, they should not also be charged with investigating and recommending the honest and capable.
translations.idiomatic: Never in antiquity did the post of supervising punishments carry exclusive authority to recommend and promote. If Your Majesty does not wish to abolish the office at once, its holders should not also be charged with investigating and recommending the honest and capable.

sentences.zh: 歲遣監察體究，仍不時選使廉訪。」

translations.literal: Each year send out surveillance commissioners for thorough investigation, and from time to time select envoys for honest visitation."
translations.idiomatic: Each year send surveillance commissioners for thorough investigation, and from time to time select envoys for honest visitation."

sentences.zh: 上從其議，於是監察體訪之使出矣。

translations.literal: The emperor followed their proposal; thereupon the surveillance and investigation envoys were sent out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted their proposal, and the surveillance and investigation envoys were dispatched.

sentences.zh: 初，匡行院於撫州，障葛將攻邊境，會西南路通事黃摑按出使烏都碗部知其謀，奔告行院為之備，迎擊障葛，敗其兵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Kuang was acting commissioner at Fuzhou, Zhangge was about to attack the border; it happened that the Southwest Circuit interpreter Huangcha Anchu, on mission to the Wuduwang tribe, learned of the plot, ran to inform the acting commission and make preparations, met Zhangge in attack, and defeated his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Kuang was acting commissioner at Fuzhou, Zhangge was about to attack the border. The Southwest Circuit interpreter Huangcha Anchu, while on mission to the Wuduwang tribe, learned of the plot, hurried back to warn the acting commission and make preparations, met Zhangge in battle, and defeated his forces.

sentences.zh: 按出與八品職，遷四官。

translations.literal: Anchu was given an eighth-rank post and advanced four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Anchu was granted an eighth-rank post and advanced four ranks.

sentences.zh: 匡遷三官。

translations.literal: Kuang was advanced three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang was advanced three ranks.

sentences.zh: 匡奏乞以所遷三官讓其兄奉禦賽一，上嘉其義，許之。

translations.literal: Kuang memorialized asking to transfer the three ranks by which he had been advanced to his elder brother, the palace attendant Saiyi; the emperor praised his righteousness and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang memorialized asking to transfer the three ranks of his advancement to his elder brother, the palace attendant Saiyi. The emperor praised his conduct and granted the request.

sentences.zh: 改樞密副使，授世襲謀克。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and granted a hereditary military commander (mouke).
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and granted a hereditary military command (mouke).

sentences.zh: 宋主相韓侂胄。

translations.literal: The Song ruler made Han Tuozhou his chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor made Han Tuozhou his chief minister.

sentences.zh: 侂胄嘗再為國使，頗知朝廷虛實。

translations.literal: Tuozhou had twice served as envoy to the Jin state and knew rather well the strengths and weaknesses of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou had twice served as envoy to the Jin court and knew its strengths and weaknesses rather well.

sentences.zh: 及為相，與蘇師旦倡議復仇，身執其咎，繕器械，增屯戍，初未敢公言征伐，乃使邊將小小寇鈔以嘗試朝廷。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister, together with Su Shidan he advocated revenge; he personally took responsibility, repaired weapons, and increased garrison troops; at first he did not dare openly speak of campaigning, but had border generals make small raids and plunder to test the court.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, he and Su Shidan advocated revenge. Tuozhou took personal responsibility, repaired weapons, and increased border garrisons. At first he did not dare speak openly of war, but had border generals launch small raids to test the Jin court's response.

sentences.zh: 泰和五年正月，入確山界奪民馬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year of Taihe they entered the Queshan border and seized the people's horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year of Taihe (1205), Song forces entered the Queshan border and seized civilian horses.

sentences.zh: 三月，焚平氏鎮，剽民財物，掠鄧州白亭巡檢家貲，持其印去。

translations.literal: In the third month they burned Pingshi town, plundered the people's goods, seized the property of the Baiting patrol inspector of Dengzhou, and carried off his seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month they burned Pingshi town, plundered civilian property, looted the household goods of the Baiting patrol inspector of Dengzhou, and carried off his seal.

sentences.zh: 遂平縣獲宋人王俊，唐州獲宋諜者李忤，俊襄陽軍卒，忤建康人。

translations.literal: Suiping County captured the Song man Wang Jun; Tangzhou captured the Song spy Li Wu; Jun was a soldier of the Xiangyang army, Wu a man of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Suiping County captured the Song soldier Wang Jun; Tangzhou captured the Song spy Li Wu. Jun was a soldier of the Xiangyang army; Wu was a native of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 俊言宋人於江州、鄂、嶽屯大兵，貯甲仗，修戰艦，期以五月入寇。

translations.literal: Jun said that the Song were stationing large forces at Jiangzhou, Ezhou, and Yuezhou, storing armor and weapons, repairing war vessels, and planned to invade in the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: Jun reported that the Song were massing troops at Jiangzhou, Ezhou, and Yuezhou, storing arms and armor, repairing warships, and planned to invade in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 忤言侂胄謂大國西北用兵連年，公私困竭，可以得志，命修建康宮，勸宋主都建康節制諸道。

translations.literal: Wu said that Tuozhou considered that the great state had waged war in the northwest for successive years and that public and private resources were exhausted, so success could be had; he ordered the Jiankang palace built and urged the Song ruler to move the capital to Jiankang to control all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Wu said that Tuozhou believed the Jin had fought in the northwest for years and that public and private resources were exhausted, so the Song could prevail. He ordered the Jiankang palace built and urged the Song emperor to move the capital to Jiankang to command all circuits.

sentences.zh: 河南統軍司奏請益兵為之備。

translations.literal: The Henan Commandery-General's office memorialized requesting additional troops for preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan Commandery-General's office memorialized for reinforcements to prepare defenses.

sentences.zh: 詔平章政事僕散揆為河南宣撫使，籍諸道兵，括戰馬，臨洮、德順、秦、鞏各置弓手四千人。

translations.literal: The emperor decreed that Grand Councilor Pusan Kui should be Henan Pacification Commissioner, muster troops from all circuits, register war horses, and place four thousand bowmen each at Lintao, Deshun, Qin, and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Grand Councilor Pusan Kui Henan Pacification Commissioner, ordered troops mustered from all circuits and war horses registered, and stationed four thousand bowmen each at Lintao, Deshun, Qin, and Gong.

sentences.zh: 詔揆遺書宋人曰：「奈何興兵？」

translations.literal: The emperor decreed that Kui send a letter to the Song, saying, "Why do you raise troops?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Kui to send a letter to the Song asking, "Why do you raise troops?"

sentences.zh: 宋人辭曰：「盜賊也。

translations.literal: The Song replied, "They were bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Song replied, "They were mere bandits.

sentences.zh: 邊臣不謹，今黜之矣。」

translations.literal: The border officials were not careful; they have now been dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Our border officials were negligent; they have now been dismissed."

sentences.zh: 宋人將啟邊釁，太常卿趙之傑、知大興府承暉、中丞孟鑄皆曰：「江南敗衄之餘，自救不暇，恐不敢敗盟。」

translations.literal: The Song were about to open a border quarrel; the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Zhao Zhijie, the Administrator of Daxing Cheng Hui, and the Censor-in-chief Meng Zhu all said, "After their defeat in the south, they have no leisure to save themselves and probably dare not break the treaty."
translations.idiomatic: With the Song about to provoke trouble on the border, Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Zhao Zhijie, Administrator of Daxing Cheng Hui, and Censor-in-chief Meng Zhu all said, "After their defeat in the south they can scarcely save themselves and probably dare not break the treaty."

sentences.zh: 匡曰：「彼置忠義保捷軍，取先世開寶、天禧紀元，豈忘中國者哉。」

translations.literal: Kuang said, "They have established the Loyal and Righteous Swift-Victory Army and taken the reign titles Kaibao and Tianxi of former times—how could they have forgotten China!"
translations.idiomatic: Kuang said, "They have established the Loyal and Righteous Swift-Victory Army and revived the reign titles Kaibao and Tianxi of former times—have they forgotten the Central Plains?"

sentences.zh: 大理卿畏也曰：「宋兵攻圍城邑，動輒數千，不得為小寇。」

translations.literal: The Minister of Justice Weiye said, "Song troops attack and besiege walled cities, numbering several thousand at a time—they cannot be called small raiders."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Weiye said, "Song troops attack and besiege walled cities by the thousands—they cannot be dismissed as small raiders."

sentences.zh: 上問參政思忠，思忠極言宋人敗盟有狀、與匡、畏也合，上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Participating Minister Sizhong; Sizhong spoke at length that the Song had clear evidence of breaking the treaty, agreeing with Kuang and Weiye; the emperor considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Participating Minister Sizhong. Sizhong argued at length that the Song had clearly broken the treaty, in agreement with Kuang and Weiye, and the emperor accepted this view.

sentences.zh: 及河南統軍使紇石烈子仁使宋還，奏宋主修敬有加，無他志。

translations.literal: When the Henan Commandery-General Heshilie Ziren returned from his mission to Song, he reported that the Song ruler showed increased respect and had no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan Commandery-General Heshilie Ziren returned from his mission to Song, he reported that the Song emperor showed heightened respect and had no other designs.

sentences.zh: 上問匡曰：「於卿何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Kuang, "What do you think of this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Kuang, "What do you make of this?"

sentences.zh: 匡曰：「子仁言是。」

translations.literal: Kuang said, "What Ziren says is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang said, "Ziren is right."

sentences.zh: 上愕然曰：「卿前議雲何，今乃中變邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor was startled and said, "What of your earlier opinion—have you now changed your mind midway?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled and said, "What of your earlier view—have you now changed your mind?"

sentences.zh: 匡徐對曰：「子仁守疆圉，不妄生事，職也。

translations.literal: Kuang answered slowly, "Ziren guards the frontier and does not lightly create incidents—that is his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang answered calmly, "Ziren guards the frontier and does not lightly create incidents—that is his duty.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰'有備無患'，在陛下宸斷耳。」

translations.literal: The Documents says, 'With preparation there is no calamity'—the decision rests with Your Majesty's sagely judgment."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, 'With preparation there is no calamity'—the decision rests with Your Majesty alone."

sentences.zh: 於是罷河南宣撫司，僕散揆還朝。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Henan Pacification Commission was abolished and Pusan Kui returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan Pacification Commission was then abolished and Pusan Kui returned to court.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，宋人陷散關，取泗州、虹縣、靈璧。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year the Song captured Sanshui Pass and took Sizhou, Hong County, and Lingbi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year the Song captured Sanshui Pass and took Sizhou, Hong County, and Lingbi.

sentences.zh: 四月，複詔僕散揆行省事於汴，制諸軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the emperor again decreed that Pusan Kui should conduct provincial affairs at Bian and control all armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the emperor again ordered Pusan Kui to conduct provincial affairs at Bian and take command of all armies.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以匡為右副元帥。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Kuang was made Right Vice Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kuang was appointed Right Vice Marshal.

sentences.zh: 揆請匡先取光州，還軍懸瓠，與大軍合勢南下。

translations.literal: Kui requested that Kuang first take Guangzhou, return the army to Xuanhu, and unite strength with the main force to march south.
translations.idiomatic: Kui asked Kuang to take Guangzhou first, then return his army to Xuanhu and join the main force for a combined advance south.

sentences.zh: 匡奏：「僕散揆大軍渡淮，宋人聚兵襄、沔以窺唐、鄧，汴京留兵頗少，有掣肘之患，請出唐、鄧。」

translations.literal: Kuang memorialized, "Pusan Kui's main force has crossed the Huai; the Song are massing troops at Xiang and Mian to spy on Tang and Deng; the troops left at Bianjing are rather few—there is the worry of being hampered; I request to advance from Tang and Deng."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang memorialized: "Pusan Kui's main army has crossed the Huai. The Song are massing at Xiang and Mian to threaten Tang and Deng, while few troops remain at Bianjing—we risk being hamstrung. I request to operate from Tang and Deng."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 遣前鋒都統烏古論慶壽以騎八千攻棗陽，遣左翼提控完顏江山以騎五千取光化，右翼都統烏古孫兀屯取神馬坡，皆克之。

translations.literal: He sent the vanguard commander-in-chief Wugulun Qingshou with eight thousand horsemen to attack Zaoyang, sent the left-wing commander Wan Yan Jiangshan with five thousand horsemen to take Guanghua, and the right-wing commander-in-chief Wugusun Wutun to take Shenmapo—all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: He sent vanguard commander Wugulun Qingshou with eight thousand cavalry against Zaoyang, left-wing commander Wanyan Jiangshan with five thousand cavalry to take Guanghua, and right-wing commander Wugusun Wutun to seize Shenmapo—all succeeded.

sentences.zh: 匡軍次白虎粒，都統完顏按帶取隨州，烏古論慶壽扼赤岸，斷襄、漢路。

translations.literal: Kuang's army halted at Baihuli; the commander-in-chief Wan Yan Andai took Suizhou; Wugulun Qingshou held Chian and cut the Xiang-Han route.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang's army encamped at Baihuli. Commander Wanyan Andai took Suizhou while Wugulun Qingshou held Chian and severed the route between Xiang and Han.

sentences.zh: 宋隨州將雷大尉遁去，遂克隨州。

translations.literal: The Song defender of Suizhou, Commandant Lei, fled, and Suizhou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Song commander of Suizhou, Commandant Lei, fled, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 於是宋鄧城、樊城戍兵皆潰。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Song garrisons at Dengcheng and Fancheng all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The Song garrisons at Dengcheng and Fancheng then collapsed.

sentences.zh: 賜詔獎諭，戒諸軍毋虜掠、焚壞城邑。

translations.literal: An edict was bestowed praising and instructing him, admonishing all armies not to plunder captives or burn and destroy walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an edict of praise and admonished all armies not to plunder or burn cities.

sentences.zh: 匡進兵圍德安，分遣諸將徇下安陸、應城、雲夢、漢川、荊山等縣，副統蒲察攻宜城縣取之。

translations.literal: Kuang advanced to besiege De'an and dispatched generals to subdue Anlu, Yingcheng, Yunmeng, Hanchuan, Jingshan, and other counties; the vice-commander Pucha attacked and took Yicheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang advanced to besiege De'an and sent generals to subdue Anlu, Yingcheng, Yunmeng, Hanchuan, Jingshan, and other counties. Vice-commander Pucha attacked and captured Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 十二月，敗宋兵二萬人於信陽之東，詔曰：「卿總師出疆屢捷，殄寇撫降，日辟土宇。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he defeated twenty thousand Song troops east of Xinyang; an edict said, "You command the army beyond the borders with repeated victories, exterminating bandits and soothing those who submit, daily expanding the territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he defeated twenty thousand Song troops east of Xinyang. An edict read: "You command our armies abroad with repeated victories, destroying the enemy and accepting surrender, daily expanding our territory.

sentences.zh: 彼恃漢、江以為險阻，箠馬而渡，如涉坦途，荊、楚削平，不為難事，雖天佑順，亦卿籌畫之效也。

translations.literal: They relied on the Han and Yangzi as barriers, yet you crossed on horseback as if on level ground; to level Jing and Chu is no difficult matter—though Heaven aids the obedient, this is also the effect of your planning.
translations.idiomatic: They trusted the Han and Yangzi as barriers, yet you crossed on horseback as if on open ground. To pacify Jing and Chu is no great difficulty. Though Heaven favors the righteous, this is also the fruit of your planning.

sentences.zh: 益宏遠圖，以副朕意。」

translations.literal: Further expand your far-reaching plans to fulfill my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Expand your grand design still further to fulfill my intent."

sentences.zh: 匡進所獲女口百人。

translations.literal: Kuang presented the hundred captive women he had taken.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang presented the hundred captive women he had taken.

sentences.zh: 詔匡權尚書右丞，行省事，右副元帥如故。

translations.literal: Kuang was decreed Acting Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, conducting provincial affairs, with his post as Right Vice Marshal unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang was appointed Acting Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat with authority to conduct provincial affairs, retaining his rank as Right Vice Marshal.

sentences.zh: 初，僕散揆初至汴，既定河南諸盜，乃購得韓侂胄族人元靚，使行間于宋。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Pusan Kui first reached Bian, after pacifying the bandits of Henan, he purchased Han Tuozhou's clansman Yuan Jing and sent him as a spy into Song territory.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Pusan Kui first reached Bian and had pacified the bandits of Henan, he obtained Han Tuozhou's clansman Yuan Jing and sent him as a spy into Song territory.

sentences.zh: 元靚渡淮，宋督視江、淮兵馬事丘灊奏之宋主。

translations.literal: Yuan Jing crossed the Huai; the Song supervisor of Jiang-Huai military affairs Qiu Kan reported this to the Song ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jing crossed the Huai, and Qiu Kan, the Song supervisor of Jiang-Huai military affairs, reported it to the Song emperor.

sentences.zh: 是時，宋主、侂胄見兵屢敗以為憂，欲乞盟無以為請，得密奏，即命遣人護元靚北歸，因請議和。

translations.literal: At that time the Song ruler and Tuozhou, seeing repeated military defeats, were anxious and wished to beg for peace but had no means to request it; receiving the secret report, they immediately ordered men to escort Yuan Jing north and thereby requested peace talks.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor and Tuozhou, alarmed by repeated defeats, wished to sue for peace but lacked a channel. On receiving the secret report they at once sent men to escort Yuan Jing north and requested negotiations.

sentences.zh: 密使其屬劉佑送元靚申和議於揆，揆曰：「稱臣割地，獻首禍之臣，然後可。」

translations.literal: They secretly had their subordinate Liu You send Yuan Jing to present the peace proposal to Kui; Kui said, "Proclaim yourselves subjects, cede territory, and present the chief culprit—only then may it be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: They secretly sent Liu You with Yuan Jing to present peace terms to Kui. Kui replied, "You must acknowledge subjection, cede territory, and hand over the chief culprit—only then can we agree."

sentences.zh: 宋主因密諭丘灊，使歸罪邊將以請焉。

translations.literal: The Song ruler thereupon secretly instructed Qiu Kan to shift blame to the border generals in making the request.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor secretly instructed Qiu Kan to blame the border generals in making the request.

sentences.zh: 及宗浩代揆，方信孺至，宗浩以方信孺輕佻不可信，移書宋人，果欲請和當遣硃致和、吳琯、李大性、李璧來。

translations.literal: When Zonghao replaced Kui and Fang Xinru arrived, Zonghao considered Fang Xinru frivolous and untrustworthy and sent a letter to the Song: if they truly wished peace they must send Zhu Zhihe, Wu Guan, Li Daxing, and Li Bi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghao replaced Kui and Fang Xinru arrived, Zonghao judged Fang Xinru frivolous and unreliable. He wrote to the Song that if they truly sought peace they must send Zhu Zhihe, Wu Guan, Li Daxing, and Li Bi.

sentences.zh: 侂胄得報大喜過望，乃召張岩于建康，罷為福建觀察使，歸罪蘇師旦，貶之嶺南。

translations.literal: Tuozhou received the reply and was delighted beyond expectation; he summoned Zhang Yan from Jiankang, dismissed him as Fujian surveillance commissioner, blamed Su Shidan, and banished him to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou received the reply with joy beyond his hopes. He summoned Zhang Yan from Jiankang, removed him to the Fujian surveillance post, blamed Su Shidan, and banished him to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 是時，李璧已為參政，不可遣。

translations.literal: At that time Li Bi was already a participating minister and could not be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi was already a participating minister and could not be sent.

sentences.zh: 硃致知、吳琯已死，李大性知福州，道遠不能遽至。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhizhi and Wu Guan were already dead; Li Daxing was prefect of Fuzhou and, the road being long, could not arrive quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhizhi and Wu Guan were already dead. Li Daxing was prefect of Fuzhou and could not arrive quickly because of the distance.

sentences.zh: 乃遣左司郎中王柟來，至濠州，匡使人責以稱臣等數事，柟以宋主、侂胄情實為請，依靖康二年正月請和故事，世為伯侄國，增歲幣為三十萬兩、匹、犒軍錢三百萬貫，蘇師旦等俟和議定當函首以獻。

translations.literal: They therefore sent Left Department Director Wang Kan; when he reached Haozhou, Kuang had men press him on submission and other matters; Kan pleaded the true situation of the Song ruler and Tuozhou, following the precedent of the peace request in the first month of the second year of Jingkang—a perpetual uncle-nephew relationship between states, increased annual tribute to three hundred thousand taels and bolts, army consolation money of three million strings—and that Su Shidan and others, once peace was settled, would be sent in coffins with their heads.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Left Department Director Wang Kan. At Haozhou, Kuang's envoys pressed him on submission and related demands. Kan pleaded the Song emperor's and Tuozhou's true position, citing the peace precedent of the first month of Jingkang 2: a perpetual uncle-nephew relationship, annual tribute raised to three hundred thousand taels and bolts, army consolation money of three million strings, and Su Shidan and others to be sent in coffins once peace was concluded.

sentences.zh: 柟至汴，以侂胄書上元帥府，匡複詰之，柟懇請曰：「此事實出朝旨，非行人所專。」

translations.literal: Kan reached Bian and presented Tuozhou's letter to the marshal's headquarters; Kuang again pressed him; Kan earnestly pleaded, "This matter truly issued from court policy—not something an envoy alone could decide."
translations.idiomatic: Kan reached Bian and presented Tuozhou's letter to headquarters. Kuang pressed him again. Kan pleaded earnestly: "This truly issued from court policy—not something an envoy alone could decide."

sentences.zh: 匡察其不妄，乃具奏。

translations.literal: Kuang perceived he was not lying and thereupon submitted a full report.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang judged that he was not lying and submitted a full report.

sentences.zh: 章宗詔匡移書宋人，當函侂胄首贖淮南地，改犒軍錢為銀三百萬兩。

translations.literal: Zhangzong decreed that Kuang send a letter to the Song: they must send Tuozhou's head in a box to ransom the Huainan lands, and the army consolation money was changed to three million taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong ordered Kuang to write to the Song: they must send Tuozhou's head in a box to ransom the Huainan territories, and the army consolation payment was changed to three million taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 於是，宋吏部侍郎史彌遠定計殺韓柟胄，彌遠知國政，和好自此成矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Song Vice Minister of Personnel Shi Miyuan devised a plan to kill Han Tuozhou; Miyuan took charge of state affairs, and peace was achieved from this point.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Song Vice Minister of Personnel Shi Miyuan devised the plan to kill Han Tuozhou. Miyuan took charge of government, and peace was concluded from that moment.

sentences.zh: 於是，廷議諸軍已取關隘不可與。

translations.literal: Thereupon at court it was debated that the passes already taken by the armies could not be returned.
translations.idiomatic: At court it was argued that the passes already taken could not be returned.

sentences.zh: 王柟以宋參政錢象祖書來，略曰：

translations.literal: Wang Kan brought a letter from the Song participating minister Qian Xiangzu, which in summary read:
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kan brought a letter from Song participating minister Qian Xiangzu, which in summary read:

sentences.zh: 竊惟昔者修好之初，蒙大金先皇帝許以畫淮為界。

translations.literal: I venture to consider that when friendly relations were first established, we received the gracious permission of the Great Jin's former emperor to take the Huai as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that when friendly relations were first established, the Great Jin's former emperor graciously permitted the Huai as our boundary.

sentences.zh: 今大國遵先皇帝聖意，自盱眙至唐、鄧畫界仍舊，是先皇帝惠之于始，今皇帝全之于後也。

translations.literal: Now the great state follows the former emperor's sacred intent, and from Xuyi to Tang and Deng the drawn boundary remains as before—this is the former emperor's grace at the beginning and the present emperor's completion at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Now the great state follows the former emperor's intent, and from Xuyi to Tang and Deng the boundary remains as before—the former emperor's grace at the start and the present emperor's completion at the end.

sentences.zh: 然東南立國，吳、蜀相依，今川、陝關隘，大國若有之，則是撤蜀之門戶，不能保蜀，何以固吳？

translations.literal: Yet the southeast established its state with Wu and Shu depending on each other; if the great state now holds the Sichuan and Shaanxi passes, this is to remove Shu's gate and barrier—unable to preserve Shu, how can Wu be secured?
translations.idiomatic: Yet our southeastern state depends on Wu and Shu supporting each other. If the great state holds the Sichuan and Shaanxi passes, you remove Shu's gate and barrier. Without securing Shu, how can Wu be held?

sentences.zh: 已增歲幣至三十萬，通謝為三百萬貫，以連歲師旅之餘，重以喪禍，豈易辦集。

translations.literal: Annual tribute has already been increased to three hundred thousand; the tribute of gratitude to three million strings—after successive years of campaigning, compounded by mourning calamity—how can this be easily assembled?
translations.idiomatic: Annual tribute has been raised to three hundred thousand, and the tribute of gratitude to three million strings. After years of war, compounded by mourning, how can this be easily assembled?

sentences.zh: 但邊隙既開和議，區區悔艾之實，不得不黽勉遵承。

translations.literal: Yet since the border quarrel has opened peace talks, the modest reality of repentance cannot but be earnestly obeyed and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now that peace talks have begun, our modest repentance cannot but be earnestly carried out.

sentences.zh: 又蒙聖畫改輸銀三百萬兩，在本朝宜不敢固違，然傾國資財，竭民膏血，恐非大金皇帝棄過圖新，兼愛南北之意也。

translations.literal: We further received the sacred decision to change payment to three million taels of silver; our court ought not stubbornly to disobey, yet to drain the state's wealth and exhaust the people's lifeblood—this perhaps is not the Great Jin emperor's intent of setting aside past faults, seeking renewal, and loving both north and south alike.
translations.idiomatic: We further received the sacred decision to pay three million taels of silver. Our court ought not stubbornly to refuse, yet to drain the treasury and exhaust the people's blood—this may not accord with the Great Jin emperor's intent to set aside the past, seek renewal, and cherish both north and south.

sentences.zh: 主上仁慈寬厚，謹守信誓，豈有意於用兵。

translations.literal: Our sovereign is benevolent and generous, carefully keeping faith with treaties—how could he intend to use arms?
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is benevolent and generous and keeps faith with treaties—he never intended war.

sentences.zh: 止緣侂胄啟釁生事，迷國罔上，以至地斯。

translations.literal: It was only because Tuozhou provoked quarrels and created incidents, bewildering the state and deceiving his superiors, that matters reached this pass.
translations.idiomatic: It was only because Tuozhou provoked conflict, misled the state, and deceived his superiors that matters came to this pass.

sentences.zh: 是以奮發英斷，大正國典，朋附之輩，誅斥靡貸。

translations.literal: Therefore with spirited resolve and decisive judgment the national statutes were greatly rectified; the clique of partisans was punished without mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore with resolute judgment he rectified the national statutes and punished the partisan clique without mercy.

sentences.zh: 今大國欲使斬送侂胄，是未知其已死也。

translations.literal: Now the great state wishes to have Tuozhou beheaded and sent—this is not knowing that he is already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Now the great state demands Tuozhou's head—this shows you do not know he is already dead.

sentences.zh: 侂胄實本庸愚，怙權輕信，有誤國事，而致侂胄誤國者，蘇師旦也。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was in truth foolish and mediocre, relying on power and lightly trusting others, and erred in state affairs; the one who caused Tuozhou to err in state affairs was Su Shidan.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was foolish and mediocre, abused his power, and erred in state affairs. The man who led Tuozhou astray was Su Shidan.

sentences.zh: 師旦既貶，侂胄尚力庇之，囑方信孺妄言已死，近推究其事，師旦已行斬首。

translations.literal: After Shidan was demoted, Tuozhou still strenuously protected him and instructed Fang Xinru falsely to say he was already dead; on recent investigation of the matter, Shidan has already been beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: After Shidan was demoted, Tuozhou still protected him and had Fang Xinru falsely report his death. On recent investigation Shidan has already been beheaded.

sentences.zh: 儻大國終惠川、陝關隘，所畫銀兩悉力祗備，師旦首函亦當傳送，以謝大國。

translations.literal: If the great state will finally grant the Sichuan and Shaanxi passes, the stipulated silver will be prepared with full effort, and Shidan's head in a box will also be transmitted to thank the great state.
translations.idiomatic: If the great state will finally return the Sichuan and Shaanxi passes, we will prepare the stipulated silver with all our strength and send Shidan's head in a box to thank the great state.

sentences.zh: 本朝與大國通好以來，譬如一家叔侄，本自協和，不幸奴婢交鬥其間，遂成嫌間。

translations.literal: Since our court and the great state have been on friendly terms, it is like one household of uncle and nephew, originally in harmony; unhappily servants and maids quarreled between them and thus estrangement arose.
translations.idiomatic: Since our courts have been on friendly terms, we have been like uncle and nephew in one household, originally in harmony. Unhappily servants quarreled between us and estrangement arose.

sentences.zh: 一旦猶子翻然改悟，斥逐奴隸，引咎謝過，則前日之嫌便可銷釋，奚必較錙銖毫末，反傷骨肉之恩乎？

translations.literal: Once the nephew suddenly turns and awakens, drives out the slaves, accepts blame and apologizes for faults—then yesterday's estrangement can be dissolved; why must one compare ounces and hairs and in turn wound the affection of flesh and bone?
translations.idiomatic: Once the nephew awakens, drives out the slaves, and accepts blame, yesterday's estrangement can be dissolved. Why compare trifles and wound the bond of kin?

sentences.zh: 惟吳、蜀相為首尾，關隘系蜀安危，望敢備奏，始終主盟，使南北遂息肩之期，四方無兵革之患，不勝通國至願。

translations.literal: Only Wu and Shu support each other head and tail; the passes concern Shu's safety— I venture to report fully, presiding over the alliance from start to finish, so that north and south may reach the time of resting their shoulders, and the four quarters be without the affliction of arms—this is the utmost wish of the whole state.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu support each other; the passes concern Shu's safety. I venture to report fully and ask that you preside over the alliance so north and south may rest from war and the realm be free of arms—this is our state's utmost wish.

sentences.zh: 是時，陝西宣撫司請增新得關隘戍兵萬人。

translations.literal: At that time the Shaanxi Pacification Commission requested ten thousand additional garrison troops for the newly taken passes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Shaanxi Pacification Commission requested ten thousand additional garrison troops for the newly taken passes.

sentences.zh: 王柟狀稟，如蒙歸川、陝關隘，韓侂胄首必當函送，遵上國之命。

translations.literal: Wang Kan's written report stated that if the Sichuan and Shaanxi passes were graciously returned, Han Tuozhou's head would certainly be sent in a box, obeying the superior state's command.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kan's report stated that if the Sichuan and Shaanxi passes were returned, Han Tuozhou's head would certainly be sent in a box in obedience to the superior state's command.

sentences.zh: 匡奏曰：「關隘之事，臣初亦惑之，今當增戍萬人，壁壘之役，饋餫之勞，費用必廣。

translations.literal: Kuang memorialized, "On the matter of the passes, your servant was at first also puzzled; now if ten thousand garrison troops are to be added, the labor of ramparts and walls and the toil of supplying provisions—the expense must be great.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang memorialized: "I too was puzzled at first about the passes. To add ten thousand garrison troops, build ramparts, and supply provisions—the expense must be enormous.

sentences.zh: 祖宗所以取者，以關隘僅能自保耳，非有益於戰也。

translations.literal: The reason our ancestors took them was that the passes can barely protect themselves—not that they are of benefit in warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestors took them because the passes can barely defend themselves—not because they aid warfare.

sentences.zh: 設能入寇，縱之平地，以鐵騎蹂之，無一得脫。

translations.literal: If they could invade, release them onto level ground and trample them with iron cavalry—not one would escape.
translations.idiomatic: If they could invade, let them onto open ground and trample them with our iron cavalry—not one would escape.

sentences.zh: 彼哀祈不已者，以前日負固尚且摧覆，今遂失之，是無一日之安也。

translations.literal: Their unceasing pleading is because formerly, though stubborn, they were still overthrown; now having lost the passes, they have not a single day's peace.
translations.idiomatic: Their endless pleading is because, though stubborn before, they were still crushed; now having lost the passes they have not a day's peace.

sentences.zh: 必謂兵力得之不可還賜，則漢上諸郡皆膏腴耕桑之地，棗陽、光化歸順之民數萬戶，較之陝右輕重可知，獨在陛下決之耳。」

translations.literal: If one insists that what was gained by military force cannot be returned, then the commanderies along the Han are all fertile fields of mulberry and grain; Zaoyang and Guanghua have tens of thousands of households who submitted—compared with the right of Shaanxi the weight is clear; it rests with Your Majesty's decision alone."
translations.idiomatic: If you insist that what force won cannot be returned, consider that the Han commanderies are fertile farmland, and Zaoyang and Guanghua alone have tens of thousands of submitting households. Compared with western Shaanxi, the balance is clear. The decision rests with Your Majesty alone."

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「侂胄渠魁，既請函首，宋之悔服，可謂誠矣。」

translations.literal: An edict replied, "Tuozhou is the ringleader; since they have requested to send his head in a box, the Song's repentance and submission may be called sincere."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Tuozhou is the ringleader. Since they offer his head in a box, the Song's repentance may be called sincere."

sentences.zh: 匡乃遣王柟還，複書曰：「宋國負渝盟之罪，自陳悔艾，主上德度如天，不忍終絕，優示訓諭，許以更成，所以覆護鎮撫之恩，至深至厚。

translations.literal: Kuang thereupon sent Wang Kan back with a reply letter: "The Song state bears the crime of breaking the treaty and has confessed repentance; the sovereign's virtue is like Heaven, unwilling to end relations finally, graciously showing instruction and admonition, permitting renewed peace—thus the grace of protection and soothing is extremely deep and thick.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang sent Wang Kan back with a reply: "The Song bear the crime of breaking the treaty and confess repentance. His Majesty's virtue is like Heaven. Unwilling to end relations, he graciously instructs and permits renewed peace—the grace of protection and soothing is profound.

sentences.zh: 昨奉聖訓，如能斬送韓侂胄，徐議還淮南地。

translations.literal: Yesterday we received the sacred instruction that if Han Tuozhou could be beheaded and sent, the Huainan lands might then be discussed for return.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday we received the sacred instruction that if Han Tuozhou were beheaded and sent, the Huainan lands might then be discussed for return.

sentences.zh: 來書言韓侂胄已死，將以蘇師旦首易之，飾辭相紿如此。

translations.literal: Your letter says Han Tuozhou is already dead and would exchange Su Shidan's head for it—embellishing words and deceiving thus.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter says Han Tuozhou is dead and offers Su Shidan's head instead—such embellished deceit.

sentences.zh: 至於犒軍銀兩欲俟歸關隘然後祗備，是皆有咈聖訓。

translations.literal: As for the army consolation silver, wishing to wait until the passes are returned before preparing it—all this contradicts the sacred instruction.
translations.idiomatic: As for the army consolation silver, wishing to wait until the passes are returned before preparing it—all this contradicts the sacred instruction.

sentences.zh: 及王柟狀稟，如蒙歸還川、陝關隘，其韓侂胄首必當函送。

translations.literal: And Wang Kan's written report stated that if the Sichuan and Shaanxi passes were graciously returned, Han Tuozhou's head would certainly be sent in a box.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kan's report also stated that if the Sichuan and Shaanxi passes were returned, Han Tuozhou's head would certainly be sent in a box.

sentences.zh: 聖訓令斬送侂胄首者，本欲易淮南地，陝西關隘不預焉。

translations.literal: The sacred instruction ordering Tuozhou's head to be beheaded and sent was originally intended to ransom the Huainan lands; the Shaanxi passes were not included.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred instruction to send Tuozhou's head was meant to ransom the Huainan lands; the Shaanxi passes were not included.

sentences.zh: 王柟所陳亦非元畫事理，不敢專決，具奏。

translations.literal: What Wang Kan stated is also not according to the original drawn principles; I dare not decide alone and submit the full report.
translations.idiomatic: What Wang Kan stated also departs from the original agreement. I dare not decide alone and submit the full report.

sentences.zh: 奉旨'朕以生靈為念，已貰宋罪，關隘區區豈足深較，既能函送韓侂胄首，陝西關隘可以還賜'。

translations.literal: Receiving the instruction: 'Considering the people, I have already pardoned the Song's crime; the petty passes are not worth deep comparison; since they can send Han Tuozhou's head in a box, the Shaanxi passes may be returned.'
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the instruction: 'Considering the people, I have pardoned the Song. The petty passes are not worth deep dispute. Since they can send Han Tuozhou's head in a box, the Shaanxi passes may be returned.'

sentences.zh: 今恩訓如此，其體大國寬仁矜恤曲從之意，追修誓書，齎遣通謝人使赴闕。」

translations.literal: Now that gracious instruction is thus, embody the great state's intent of generous benevolence and compassionate yielding, revise the oath document, and send the envoy of gratitude to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Now that this gracious instruction is given, embody the great state's generous and compassionate intent, revise the oath document, and send the envoy of gratitude to court."

sentences.zh: 王柟之歸也，匡要以先送叛亡驅掠，然後割賜淮南、川、陝，及彼誓書草本有犯廟諱字及文義有不如體制者，諭令改之。

translations.literal: When Wang Kan returned, Kuang required that rebel fugitives and plundered captives be sent first, and only then would Huainan, Sichuan, and Shaanxi be ceded; moreover, where their draft oath document contained taboo characters against the temple names or where the literary sense did not accord with proper form, they were instructed to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Kan returned, Kuang required rebel fugitives and plundered captives to be sent first, and only then would Huainan, Sichuan, and Shaanxi be ceded. Where their draft oath contained taboo characters or improper wording, they were instructed to revise it.

sentences.zh: 宋人以叛亡驅掠散在州縣，一旦拘刷，未易聚集。

translations.literal: The Song said the rebel fugitives and plundered captives were scattered among prefectures and counties and could not easily be gathered if seized all at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Song replied that rebel fugitives and plundered captives were scattered among prefectures and counties and could not easily be gathered at once.

sentences.zh: 今已四月，農事已晚，邊民連歲流離失所，扶攜道路，即望複業，過此農時，遂失一歲之望。

translations.literal: It is already the fourth month and the farming season is late; border people for successive years have been displaced and lost their homes, supporting one another on the roads and hoping immediately to resume their livelihoods—past this farming season, they lose the hope of a year's harvest.
translations.idiomatic: It is already the fourth month and the farming season is late. Border people have been displaced for years and hope to resume their livelihoods. Past this season they lose a year's harvest.

sentences.zh: 歲幣犒軍物多，非旬月可辦。

translations.literal: The annual tribute and army consolation goods are many and cannot be prepared in a month or ten days.
translations.idiomatic: The annual tribute and army consolation goods are many and cannot be prepared in a month or two.

sentences.zh: 錢象祖複以書來，略曰：「竊見大金皇帝前日聖旨，如能斬送韓侂胄首，沿淮之地並依皇統、大定已畫為定。

translations.literal: Qian Xiangzu again sent a letter, which in summary read: "I have seen the Great Jin emperor's earlier sacred instruction that if Han Tuozhou's head could be beheaded and sent, the lands along the Huai would all follow the boundaries drawn in Huangtong and Dading.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiangzu sent another letter, which in summary read: "I have seen the Great Jin emperor's earlier instruction that if Han Tuozhou's head were sent, the lands along the Huai would follow the Huangtong and Dading boundaries.

sentences.zh: 又睹今來聖旨，既能送侂胄首，陝西關隘可並還賜。

translations.literal: I have also seen the present sacred instruction that since Tuozhou's head can be sent, the Shaanxi passes may also be returned together.
translations.idiomatic: I have also seen the present instruction that since Tuozhou's head can be sent, the Shaanxi passes may also be returned.

sentences.zh: 以此仰見聖慈寬大，初無必待發遣驅掠官兵，然後退兵交界之語。

translations.literal: From this I look up and perceive sacred compassion and generosity; there was originally no language requiring that plundered troops and captives be dispatched first before withdrawing troops to the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: From this I perceive sacred compassion; there was never a requirement that plundered troops and captives be sent before withdrawing to the boundary.

sentences.zh: 誓書草本添改處，先次錄本齎呈，並將侂胄首函送，及管押納合、道僧、李全家口一併發還。

translations.literal: The additions and revisions to the draft oath document are first copied and presented; Tuozhou's head in a box will also be sent, and the households of Nahe, Daoseng, and Li Quan under guard will be dispatched back together.
translations.idiomatic: The revisions to the draft oath are copied and presented first. Tuozhou's head in a box will be sent, and the households of Nahe, Daoseng, and Li Quan under guard will be returned together.

sentences.zh: 欲望上體大金皇帝畫定聖旨，先賜行下沿邊及陝西所屬，候侂胄首至界上，即便抽回軍馬，歸還淮南及川、陝關隘地界。

translations.literal: We desire to embody the Great Jin emperor's drawn and fixed sacred instruction, first grant orders down to the border regions and Shaanxi dependencies; when Tuozhou's head reaches the boundary, immediately withdraw the armies and return the Huainan and Sichuan-Shaanxi pass territories.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that you embody the Great Jin emperor's fixed instruction, issue orders to the border regions and Shaanxi dependencies, and when Tuozhou's head reaches the boundary, immediately withdraw the armies and return Huainan and the Sichuan-Shaanxi passes.

sentences.zh: 所有驅掠官兵，留之何益，見已從實刷勘，發還，其使人禮物歲幣等已起發至真、揚間，伺候嘉報，迤邐前去界首，以俟取接。」

translations.literal: As for all plundered troops and captives, what use is keeping them—they have already been truthfully checked and sent back; the envoy's gifts, annual tribute, and the like have already been dispatched to between Zhen and Yang, awaiting favorable reply, proceeding gradually to the boundary to await reception."
translations.idiomatic: As for plundered troops and captives, what use is keeping them—they have been checked and sent back. The envoy's gifts and annual tribute have been dispatched toward Zhen and Yang, awaiting your favorable reply, and will proceed gradually to the boundary for reception."

sentences.zh: 匡得錢象祖書，即具奏，詔報曰：「朕以生靈之故，已從所請，稱臣割地，尚且闊略，區區小節，何足深較。

translations.literal: Kuang received Qian Xiangzu's letter and immediately submitted a full report; an edict replied, "For the sake of the people I have already granted what was requested; submission and ceding territory were still treated leniently—petty small matters are not worth deep comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang received Qian Xiangzu's letter and submitted a full report. An edict replied: "For the people's sake I have granted what was requested. Even submission and ceding territory were treated leniently—petty matters are not worth deep dispute.

sentences.zh: 其侂胄、師旦首函及諸叛亡至濠州，即聽通謝人使入界，軍馬即當徹還，川、陝關隘，俟歲幣犒軍銀綱至下蔡，畫日割賜。」

translations.literal: When the boxes with the heads of Tuozhou and Shidan and all rebel fugitives reach Haozhou, immediately permit the envoy of gratitude to enter the border; the armies should at once be fully withdrawn; the Sichuan and Shaanxi passes, when the annual tribute and army consolation silver arrive at Xia Cai, will be ceded on a fixed day."
translations.idiomatic: When the boxes with Tuozhou's and Shidan's heads and all rebel fugitives reach Haozhou, permit the envoy of gratitude to enter the border at once and withdraw the armies. The Sichuan and Shaanxi passes will be ceded on a fixed day when the annual tribute and army consolation silver reach Xia Cai."

sentences.zh: 匡得詔書，即以諭宋人，使如詔書從事。

translations.literal: Kuang received the edict and immediately informed the Song to act according to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang received the edict and informed the Song to act accordingly.

sentences.zh: 泰和八年閏四月乙未，宋獻韓侂胄、蘇師旦首函至元帥府，匡遣平南撫軍上將軍紇石烈貞以，侂胄、師旦首函露布以聞。

translations.literal: On the yimao day of the intercalary fourth month of the eighth year of Taihe, the Song presented the boxes with the heads of Han Tuozhou and Su Shidan to the marshal's headquarters; Kuang dispatched the Pacification General of the South, Senior General Heshilie Zhenyi, to announce by bulletin the heads of Tuozhou and Shidan.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day of the intercalary fourth month of the eighth year of Taihe (1208), the Song presented the boxes with the heads of Han Tuozhou and Su Shidan to headquarters. Kuang dispatched Pacification General of the South Heshilie Zhenyi to announce the news by bulletin.

sentences.zh: 五月丁未，遣戶部尚書高汝礪、禮部尚書張行簡奏告天地，武衛軍都指揮使徒單鏞奏告太廟，禦史中丞孟鑄告社稷。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day of the fifth month he dispatched the Minister of Revenue Gao Rushi and the Minister of Rites Zhang Xingjian to report to Heaven and Earth; the Commander-in-chief of the Martial Guard Army Tudan Yong to report to the Grand Temple; and the Censor-in-chief Meng Zhu to report to the Altars of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the fifth month he dispatched Minister of Revenue Gao Rushi and Minister of Rites Zhang Xingjian to report to Heaven and Earth, Martial Guard commander Tudan Yong to report to the Grand Temple, and Censor-in-chief Meng Zhu to the Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 是日，上禦應天門，立黃麾仗，受宋馘。

translations.literal: That day the emperor proceeded to the Gate of Responding Heaven, established the yellow-banner guard, and received the Song war trophies.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor proceeded to the Gate of Responding Heaven, established the imperial guard, and received the Song war trophies.

sentences.zh: 尚書省奏露布，親王百官起居上表稱賀。

translations.literal: The Secretariat reported the bulletin; imperial princes and all officials performed obeisance and submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat reported the bulletin. Imperial princes and officials performed obeisance and submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 獻馘廟社，以露布頒中外。

translations.literal: The war trophies were presented to the temples and altars, and the bulletin was promulgated within and without.
translations.idiomatic: The war trophies were presented to the temples and altars, and the bulletin was promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 竿侂胄、師旦首並二人畫像于通衢，百姓縱觀，然後漆其首，藏之軍器庫。

translations.literal: The heads of Tuozhou and Shidan and portraits of the two men were raised on poles in the public thoroughfare for the people to view freely; then their heads were lacquered and stored in the armory.
translations.idiomatic: The heads of Tuozhou and Shidan and their portraits were displayed on poles in the public thoroughfare for the people to view. Their heads were then lacquered and stored in the armory.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，匡朝京師，進官兩階，賜玉帶、金一百兩、銀一千五百兩，重幣三十端。

translations.literal: On the bingchen day Kuang attended court at the capital, was advanced two ranks, and was bestowed a jade belt, one hundred taels of gold, fifteen hundred taels of silver, and thirty bolts of heavy silks.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day Kuang attended court at the capital, was advanced two ranks, and received a jade belt, one hundred taels of gold, fifteen hundred taels of silver, and thirty bolts of heavy silks.

sentences.zh: 罷元帥府仍為樞密院。

translations.literal: The marshal's headquarters was abolished and restored as the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal's headquarters was abolished and restored as the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六月癸酉，宋通謝使許弈、吳衡等入見。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day of the sixth month the Song envoys of gratitude Xu Yi, Wu Heng, and others were received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the sixth month the Song envoys of gratitude Xu Yi, Wu Heng, and others were received in audience.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以宋人請和詔天下。

translations.literal: On the guiwei day an edict was issued to the realm on the Song people's request for peace.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day an edict announced to the realm the Song request for peace.

sentences.zh: 匡事顯宗，深被恩遇。

translations.literal: Kuang served Xianzong and was deeply favored.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang served Xianzong and enjoyed deep favor.

sentences.zh: 自章宗幼年，侍講讀最親幸，致位將相，怙寵自用，官以賄成。

translations.literal: From Zhangzong's youth he was the most intimately favored tutor and reader; reaching the rank of general and minister, he relied on favor and acted on his own; offices were obtained through bribes.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhangzong's youth he was the most favored tutor. Rising to general and minister, he relied on favor and acted arbitrarily; offices were bought with bribes.

sentences.zh: 承安中，撥賜家口地土，匡乃自占濟南、真定、代州上腴田，百姓舊業輒奪之，及限外自取。

translations.literal: In the Cheng'an era, when household lands were allotted and granted, Kuang himself seized fertile fields in Jinan, Zhending, and Daizhou, snatching the people's old holdings and taking beyond the allotted limits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Cheng'an era, when household lands were allotted, Kuang seized fertile fields in Jinan, Zhending, and Daizhou, snatching commoners' holdings and taking beyond his allotment.

sentences.zh: 上聞其事，不以為罪，惟用安州邊吳泊舊放圍埸地、奉聖州在官閒田易之，以向自占者悉還百姓。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of the matter he did not treat it as a crime, but only exchanged them for the old hunting grounds at Wu Bo on the Anzhou border and idle official fields at Fengshengzhou, returning all that Kuang had seized to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he did not punish him but exchanged the lands for old hunting grounds at Wu Bo on the Anzhou border and idle official fields at Fengshengzhou, returning all Kuang had seized to the people.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘗謂侍臣曰：「撒速往年嘗受人玉吐鶻，然後與之官，此豈宰相所為哉？」

translations.literal: Xuanzong once said to the attendants, "Sasu in former years accepted a jade hawk from someone and only then gave him an office—is this what a chief minister should do?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong once told his attendants, "Sasu once accepted a jade hawk from someone and only then gave him an office—is that what a chief minister should do?"

sentences.zh: 完顏綱

translations.literal: Wan Yan Gang
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Gang

sentences.zh: 完顏綱，本名元奴，字正甫。

translations.literal: Wan Yan Gang, original name Yuannu, style name Zhengfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Gang, whose original name was Yuannu and style name Zhengfu.

sentences.zh: 明昌中，為奉禦，累官左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the Mingchang era he served as palace attendant and rose through offices to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mingchang era he served as palace attendant and rose to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 詔三叉口置捺缽。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a naboo to be established at Sanchakou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a naboo relay station established at Sanchakou.

sentences.zh: 綱上疏諫，疏中有雲：「賊出沒其間」，詔尚書省詰問，所言不實，章宗以綱諫官，不之罪。

translations.literal: Gang submitted a memorial of remonstrance in which he wrote, "Bandits appear and disappear in that region"; the emperor decreed the Secretariat to investigate; what he said was not true; Zhangzong, because Gang was a remonstrance official, did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Gang submitted a memorial of remonstrance stating that "bandits appear and disappear in that region." The emperor ordered the Secretariat to investigate. His claim proved false, but Zhangzong, because Gang was a remonstrance official, did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部員外郎，綱言：「諸犯死罪除名移推相去二百里，並犯徒罪連逮二十人以上者並令就問，曾經所屬按察司審讞者移推別路，官亦依上就問。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments; Gang said, "For all condemned to death, removal from office, and transfer for trial where the distance is two hundred li, and for those implicated in penal servitude involving twenty persons or more—all should be questioned on the spot; those already tried by the surveillance commission of their circuit should be transferred to another circuit; officials should likewise be questioned on the spot as above.
