translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments, Gang proposed: "For capital cases involving removal from office and transfer for trial within two hundred li, and for penal-servitude cases implicating twenty or more persons—all should be tried on the spot. Cases already tried by the local surveillance commission should be transferred to another circuit. Officials should likewise be tried on the spot.

sentences.zh: 凡告移推之人皆已經本路按察審訖，即當移推別路。

translations.literal: All persons reported for transfer trial have already been tried and concluded by the surveillance commission of their circuit and should be transferred to another circuit.
translations.idiomatic: All persons reported for transfer have already been tried by their circuit's surveillance commission and should be transferred to another circuit.

sentences.zh: 按察司部分廣闊，如上京路移推臨潢路，最近亦往復二三千里，北京留守司移推西北路招討司，最近亦須數月。

translations.literal: The surveillance commissions' jurisdictions are vast and broad; for example, transferring from the Shangjing circuit to the Linhuang circuit requires at least two or three thousand li round trip; transferring from the Beijing regency to the Northwest Circuit Pacification Commission requires at least several months even at the nearest.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissions cover vast territories. Transferring a case from the Shangjing circuit to the Linhuang circuit requires a round trip of at least two or three thousand li. Transferring from the Beijing regency to the Northwest Circuit Pacification Commission takes months even at the nearest point.

sentences.zh: 乞依舊制，令移推官司追取其人歸問。」

translations.literal: He requested that under the former regulations transfer-trial offices be ordered to pursue and bring back the persons for questioning."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that under the old system the transfer-trial authorities be ordered to pursue the accused and bring them back for interrogation."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 六年，與宋連兵，陝西諸將頗相異同，以綱為蜀漢路安撫使、都大提舉兵馬事，與元帥府參決西事，調羌兵之未附者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year war continued with Song; the generals of Shaanxi differed greatly among themselves. Gang was made Pacification Commissioner of the Shu-Han Circuit and Grand Commissioner for Military Affairs, to join the Marshal's headquarters in deciding western affairs and to mobilize Qiang troops not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, while war with Song continued, Shaanxi's generals were deeply divided. Gang was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Shu-Han Circuit and Grand Commissioner for Military Affairs, to deliberate western strategy with the Marshal's headquarters and to rally unaffiliated Qiang forces.

sentences.zh: 於是，知鳳翔府事完顏昱、同知平涼府事蒲察秉鉉分駐鳳翔諸隘，通遠軍節度使承裕、秦州防禦使完顏璘屯成紀界，知臨洮府事石抹仲溫駐臨洮，同知臨洮府事術虎高琪、彰化軍節度副使把回海備鞏州諸鎮，乾州刺史完顏思忠扼六盤，陝西路都統副使斡勒牙刺、京兆府推官蒲察秉彝戍虢華、扼潼關蒲津，陝西都統完顏忠本名嫋懶、同知京兆府事烏古論兗州守京兆要害，以鳳翔、臨洮路蕃漢弓箭手及緋翮翅軍散據邊陲。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wan Yan Yu, prefect of Fengxiang, and Pucha Bingxian, vice-prefect of Pingliang, were posted separately at Fengxiang's passes; Cheng Yu, military commissioner of Tongyuan, and Wan Yan Lin, defense commissioner of Qinzhou, encamped on the Chengji frontier; Shimo Zhongwen, prefect of Lintao, was stationed at Lintao; Shuhu Gaoqi, vice-prefect of Lintao, and Ba Huihai, vice-commissioner of the Zhanghua army, prepared the forts of Gongzhou; Wan Yan Sizhong, prefect of Qianzhou, held Liupan; Wolian Yaci, vice commander-in-chief of the Shaanxi circuit, and Pucha Bingyi, investigating official of Jingzhao, garrisoned Guohua and held Tong Pass and the Pujin crossing; Wan Yan Zhong (original name Niaolan), commander-in-chief of Shaanxi, and Wugulun Yanzhou, vice-prefect of Jingzhao, guarded the key points of Jingzhao; the Fan and Han archers of the Fengxiang and Lintao circuits and the Feihuchi army were scattered along the border marches.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Yu, prefect of Fengxiang, and Pucha Bingxian, vice-prefect of Pingliang, took separate posts at Fengxiang's passes. Cheng Yu, commissioner of Tongyuan, and Wanyan Lin, defense commissioner of Qinzhou, encamped on the Chengji border. Shimo Zhongwen held Lintao. Shuhu Gaoqi and Ba Huihai of the Zhanghua army secured Gongzhou's forts. Wanyan Sizhong of Qianzhou blocked Liupan. Wolian Yaci and Pucha Bingyi garrisoned Guohua and held Tong Pass and Pujin. Commander Wanyan Zhong (born Niaolan) and Wugulun Yanzhou, vice-prefect of Jingzhao, held the capital region's vital points. Fan and Han archers of Fengxiang and Lintao and the Feihuchi army were spread along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 緋翮翅，軍名也。

translations.literal: Feihuchi—the name of an army.
translations.idiomatic: Feihuchi was the name of a military unit.

sentences.zh: 元帥右臨軍充右都監蒲察貞分總其事。

translations.literal: Pucha Zhen, Right Supervisor of the Marshal's Right Flank Army serving as Right Supervisor-in-Chief, was appointed to oversee the whole in divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Zhen, Right Supervisor of the Marshal's Right Flank Army acting as Right Supervisor-in-Chief, took overall charge in sections.

sentences.zh: 宋吳曦以兵六千攻鹽川，鞏州戍將完顏王善、隊校僕散六斤、猛安龍延常擊走之，斬首二百級。

translations.literal: The Song general Wu Xi led six thousand troops to attack Yanchuan. The Gongzhou garrison commander Wan Yan Wangshan, company commander Pusan Liujin, and meng'an Long Yanchang repulsed them and took two hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi of Song attacked Yanchuan with six thousand men. Gongzhou's garrison commander Wanyan Wangshan, company commander Pusan Liujin, and meng'an Long Yanchang drove him off and took two hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 七月，吳曦兵五萬由保坌、姑蘇等路寇秦州，承裕、璘以騎千餘擊之，曦兵大敗，追奔四十里。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Wu Xi led fifty thousand troops by the routes of Baoben and Gusu to raid Qinzhou. Cheng Yu and Lin with a little over a thousand cavalry attacked; Wu Xi's army was utterly defeated and pursued for forty li.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wu Xi marched fifty thousand men against Qinzhou by Baoben and Gusu. Cheng Yu and Lin struck with just over a thousand horsemen. Wu Xi was routed and pursued forty li.

sentences.zh: 曦別兵萬人入來遠鎮，術虎高琪破之。

translations.literal: Wu Xi's detached force of ten thousand entered Laiyuan Fort; Shuhu Gaoqi defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand of Wu Xi's troops entered Laiyuan Fort; Shuhu Gaoqi destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 青宜可者，吐蕃之種也。

translations.literal: Qingyi Ke was of Tibetan stock.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyi Ke was of Tibetan descent.

sentences.zh: 宋取河湟，夏取河西四郡，部落散處西鄙，其魯黎族帥曰冷京，據古疊州，有四十三族、十四城、三十余萬戶，東鄰宕昌，北接臨洮、積石，南行十日至筍竹大山，蓋蠻境也。

translations.literal: When Song took He-Huang and Xia took the four commanderies of Hexi, tribes were scattered on the western marches. The chief of the Luli tribe, named Lengjing, held ancient Diezhou with forty-three tribes, fourteen walled towns, and more than three hundred thousand households. To the east it bordered Danchang; to the north it adjoined Lintao and Jishi; to the south, ten days' march brought one to Great Bamboo Mountain in barbarian territory.
translations.idiomatic: After Song seized He-Huang and Xia took Hexi's four commanderies, tribes scattered along the western frontier. Lengjing, chief of the Luli people, held ancient Diezhou: forty-three tribes, fourteen walled towns, and over three hundred thousand households. Danchang lay to the east; Lintao and Jishi to the north; ten days south lay Great Bamboo Mountain in barbarian lands.

sentences.zh: 西行四十日至河外，俗不論道裏，而以日計之雲。

translations.literal: Forty days west lay lands beyond the river; custom did not reckon distance in li but counted by days, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Forty days west lay country beyond the river. Locals reckoned distance not in li but in days' travel.

sentences.zh: 冷京卒，子耳骨延嗣，宋不能制，縻以官爵。

translations.literal: When Lengjing died his son Erguyan succeeded. Song could not control him and kept him in check with titles and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Lengjing died and his son Erguyan succeeded. Song could not subdue him and bound him with offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 傳六世至青宜可，尤勁勇得眾，以宋政令不常，有改事中國之意。

translations.literal: The line passed through six generations to Qingyi Ke, who was especially fierce and brave and won the people. Because Song's government orders were inconstant, he harbored thoughts of turning to serve the Central Court.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations later came Qingyi Ke, fiercest and boldest of all, who won his people's hearts. Song's shifting policies stirred his wish to serve the Central Court.

sentences.zh: 曹佛留為洮州刺史。

translations.literal: Cao Foliu was prefect of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Foliu served as prefect of Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 佛留材武有智策，能結諸羌。

translations.literal: Foliu was talented in martial arts and possessed stratagems; he could unite the various Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Foliu was martial and resourceful and could rally the Qiang tribes.

sentences.zh: 青宜可畏慕佛留，以父呼之，請舉國內附。

translations.literal: Qingyi Ke feared and admired Foliu, called him father, and asked to bring the whole nation to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyi Ke revered Foliu, addressed him as father, and asked to submit his entire people.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以宋有盟不許，厚賜金帛以撫之。

translations.literal: The court, because Song had a treaty, did not permit it but richly bestowed gold and silks to placate him.
translations.idiomatic: The court, bound by treaty with Song, refused but sent rich gifts of gold and silk to appease him.

sentences.zh: 明昌間，屬羌已彪殺郡佐反，是時綱為奉禦，奉詔與曹佛留計事，因召青宜可會兵擊破已彪。

translations.literal: In the Mingchang era the dependent Qiang chief Yi Biao killed the prefectural aide and rebelled. At that time Gang was palace attendant; ordered by edict he joined Cao Foliu in planning, summoned Qingyi Ke to meet troops and defeated Yi Biao.
translations.idiomatic: During Mingchang the Qiang chief Yi Biao murdered a prefectural aide and rebelled. Gang, then a palace attendant, was ordered to plan with Cao Foliu, summoned Qingyi Ke's forces, and crushed Yi Biao.

sentences.zh: 曹佛留遷同知臨洮尹，兼洮州刺史。

translations.literal: Cao Foliu was transferred to vice-prefect of Lintao and concurrently prefect of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Foliu was promoted to vice-prefect of Lintao while retaining the Taozhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子普賢為洮州管內巡檢使。

translations.literal: His son Puxian was patrol inspector within Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Puxian became patrol inspector of Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 綱屢以事至洮，佛留每謂綱言青宜可願內屬，出其至情，綱輒奏之，上終不納。

translations.literal: Gang often came to Taozhou on business; Foliu would always tell Gang that Qingyi Ke wished to submit inward, revealing his utmost sincerity; Gang would memorialize it but the emperor ultimately did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gang's duties brought him to Taozhou, Foliu assured him of Qingyi Ke's sincere wish to submit. Gang memorialized again and again, but the throne never consented.

sentences.zh: 及綱部署陝西，上密敕經略西事。

translations.literal: When Gang deployed in Shaanxi the emperor secretly decreed him to oversee western affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gang took command in Shaanxi, the emperor secretly charged him to direct the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 於是，曹佛留已死，普賢為懷羌巡檢使。

translations.literal: By then Cao Foliu had died; Puxian was patrol inspector of Huai Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: By then Foliu was dead and Puxian served as patrol inspector of Huai Qiang.

sentences.zh: 綱至洮，馳召普賢攝同知洮州事。

translations.literal: Gang reached Taozhou and urgently summoned Puxian to act as vice-prefect of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gang reached Taozhou and urgently summoned Puxian to serve as acting vice-prefect.

sentences.zh: 普賢傳箭入羌中，青宜可大喜，率諸部長，籍其境土人民，詣綱請內屬。

translations.literal: Puxian sent arrows through the Qiang lands; Qingyi Ke was greatly pleased, led the various chieftains, registered his territory's land and people, and came to Gang requesting submission.
translations.idiomatic: Puxian sent messengers through the Qiang country. Qingyi Ke rejoiced, gathered his chiefs, registered lands and people, and came to Gang to swear allegiance.

sentences.zh: 綱奏其事，上以青宜可為疊州副都總管，加廣威將軍。

translations.literal: Gang memorialized the matter; the emperor appointed Qingyi Ke vice overall commander of Diezhou and promoted him to General of Expansive Might.
translations.idiomatic: Gang reported the submission. The emperor made Qingyi Ke vice overall commander of Diezhou and General of Expansive Might.

sentences.zh: 詔青宜可曰：「卿統有部人，世為雄長，向風慕義，背偽歸朝，願效純誠，恆輸忠力，緬懷嘉矚，式厚褒旌。

translations.literal: An edict to Qingyi Ke read: "You command your tribes and for generations have been a mighty chief. Turning toward righteousness and spurning the false regime, you wish to show pure loyalty and ever offer faithful service. We cherish your admirable intent and shall reward it generously.
translations.idiomatic: The edict to Qingyi Ke ran: "You rule your people, long a power on the frontier. Turning from the false Song toward our court, you offer steadfast loyalty. We mark your merit and will honor you richly.

sentences.zh: 覽卿進上所受偽牌，朝廷之馭諸蕃固無此例，欲使卿有以鎮撫部族、增重觀望，是以特加改命，賜金牌一、銀牌二，到可祗承，服我新恩，永為籓衛。」

translations.literal: Reviewing the false credentials you presented, the court's governance of the frontier peoples has no precedent for this; wishing you to have means to pacify your tribes and add weight to their regard, we therefore specially renew your appointment, bestowing one gold tablet and two silver tablets. On receipt you may accept them, wear our new favor, and forever guard the border as a vassal."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Song credentials you surrendered—our rule over frontier peoples knows no such precedent—we grant a new appointment so you may govern your tribes with added standing: one gold tablet and two silver. Receive them, accept our grace, and guard the marches forever."

sentences.zh: 曹普賢真授同知洮州事，綱遷拱衛直都指揮使，遷三階，安撫，都大提舉如故。

translations.literal: Cao Puxian was formally appointed vice-prefect of Taozhou; Gang was transferred to commander of the Archer's Guard and advanced three ranks, his posts as pacification commissioner and grand military commissioner unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Puxian was confirmed vice-prefect of Taozhou. Gang was made commander of the Archer's Guard, advanced three ranks, and kept his pacification and military posts.

sentences.zh: 以商州刺史烏古論兗州領、曹普賢押領、青宜可勾當。

translations.literal: Wugulun Yanzhou of Shangzhou was made leader, Cao Puxian deputy leader, and Qingyi Ke coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Yanzhou of Shangzhou led the effort, Cao Puxian served as deputy, and Qingyi Ke as coordinator.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「完顏綱，初行時汝未知朝廷有青宜可之事，獨言可以招撫，必獲其用，既而果來效順。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Wan Yan Gang, when you first set out you did not know the court already had dealings with Qingyi Ke. You alone said he could be won over and would surely prove useful—and indeed he has come to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Wanyan Gang, when you departed you did not yet know of Qingyi Ke. You alone insisted he could be won—and he has indeed submitted.

sentences.zh: 今汝勿以青宜可兵勢重大，卑屈失體，亦勿以蕃部而藐視之。」

translations.literal: Now do not, because Qingyi Ke's forces are great, demean yourself with excessive humility; nor because he is a frontier people look down on him."
translations.idiomatic: Do not humble yourself before his strength, nor despise him because he is a frontier chief."

sentences.zh: 九月，詔安慰陝西，略曰：「京兆、鳳翔、臨洮三路，應被宋兵逼脅，背國從偽，或沒落外境，若能自歸者，官吏依舊勾當，百姓各令複業，元拋地土依數給付。

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict comforted Shaanxi, in summary: "On the Jingzhao, Fengxiang, and Lintao circuits, all who were coerced by Song troops, turned from the state to follow the false regime, or were lost beyond the border—if they return of themselves, officials shall resume their posts and commoners shall return to their occupations; original lands abandoned shall be restored in full.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict reassured Shaanxi: "Those on the Jingzhao, Fengxiang, and Lintao circuits who, pressed by Song armies, followed the false regime or fled beyond the border—if they return willingly, officials keep their posts and commoners their livelihoods; abandoned lands shall be fully restored.

sentences.zh: 及受宋人旗榜結構等，或值驚擾因而避役逃亡，未發覺者，許令所在官司陳首，並行釋免，更不追究，軍前可用之人隨宜任使。

translations.literal: As for those who received Song banners and placards to organize resistance, or fled conscription in panic before discovery—let them confess at local offices and all shall be pardoned without further inquiry; men fit for the front may be employed as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Those who took Song banners, fled draft or panic, and have not been caught may confess locally and be pardoned without penalty. Able men may serve at the front as needed.

sentences.zh: 限外不首，複罪如初。

translations.literal: After the deadline, those who do not confess shall be punished as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the deadline, non-confessors face the original penalties.

sentences.zh: 宋程松遣別將曲昌世襲方山原，自率兵數萬分道襲和尚原、西山寨、龍門等關。

translations.literal: Song Cheng Song sent his deputy Qu Changshi to raid Fangshanyuan while he himself led tens of thousands in separate columns against Heshangyuan, Xishan Stockade, Longmen, and other passes.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Song of Song sent Qu Changshi to strike Fangshanyuan while he led tens of thousands against Heshangyuan, Xishan Stockade, Longmen, and other passes.

sentences.zh: 是日，大霧四塞，既又暴雨，和尚原、西山寨，龍門關戍兵不知宋兵來，松遂據之。

translations.literal: That day dense fog filled the four quarters, then torrential rain fell. The garrisons at Heshangyuan, Xishan Stockade, and Longmen Pass did not know Song troops had come, and Cheng Song seized them.
translations.idiomatic: Fog sealed the passes, then rain burst. Garrisons at Heshangyuan, Xishan, and Longmen never saw the Song coming until Cheng Song held them.

sentences.zh: 蒲察貞遣行軍副統裴滿阿裏、同知隴州事完顏孛論以兵千人伏方山原下，萬戶奧屯撒合門、美原縣令術虎合遝別將壯士五百，取間道潛登，出宋兵上，自高而下，宋兵大駭，伏兵合擊，遂破之。

translations.literal: Pucha Zhen sent the campaigning vice-commander Peiman Ali and Wan Yan Bolun, vice-prefect of Longzhou, with a thousand troops to lie in wait below Fangshanyuan; the commander of ten thousand households Aotun Sahemen and the magistrate of Meiyuan Shuhu Hedao with five hundred picked men took a hidden path and climbed above the Song army, striking from the heights. The Song were terrified; the ambush closed and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Zhen sent Peiman Ali and Wanyan Bolun with a thousand men to ambush below Fangshanyuan. Sahemen and Shuhu Hedao led five hundred up a secret path above the Song. The enemy panicked; the trap closed and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 貞乃分遣術虎合遝、部將完顏出軍奴率兵千人出黃兒谷取和尚原，同知會州事女奚列南家、押軍猛安粘割撒改率兵千人出大寧穀取西山寨，貞自以兵七百由中路取龍門等關。

translations.literal: Zhen then sent Shuhu Hedao and the officer Wan Yan Chujunu with a thousand troops out Huang'er Valley to retake Heshangyuan; Nüxi Lie Nanjia, vice-prefect of Huizhou, and the meng'an Nianhe Sagai with a thousand out Daning Valley for Xishan Stockade; Zhen himself with seven hundred took the central route for Longmen and other passes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen dispatched Hedao and Wanyan Chujunu through Huang'er Valley toward Heshangyuan; Nanjia and Sagai through Daning Valley for Xishan; Zhen himself took seven hundred along the middle road for Longmen.

sentences.zh: 程松已焚閣道，貞且修道且進兵。

translations.literal: Cheng Song had already burned the plank roads; Zhen repaired the road even as he advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Song had burned the plankways; Zhen rebuilt as he marched.

sentences.zh: 至小關，松將楊廷據險注射，貞不得前，令行軍副統裴滿阿裏為疑兵，潛遣猛安胡信率甲士五十人繞出其後，反擊之，宋兵大亂，遂斬廷於陣。

translations.literal: At Xiaoguan the Song general Yang Ting held the heights and shot down; Zhen could not advance. He ordered Peiman Ali to make a feint and secretly sent the meng'an Hu Xin with fifty armored men around behind to counterattack. The Song army fell into chaos and Ting was beheaded in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaoguan Yang Ting held the heights and rained arrows. Zhen feinted with Peiman Ali while Hu Xin circled fifty armored men behind. The Song broke; Ting fell in the melee.

sentences.zh: 宋兵走二里關，複敗。

translations.literal: The Song army fled to Erliguan and was defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: They fled to Erliguan and were beaten again.

sentences.zh: 宋將彭統領宋兵走龍門，追擊，大破之。

translations.literal: The Song commander Peng led troops toward Longmen; pursuit broke them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Peng fled toward Longmen; pursuit annihilated his force.

sentences.zh: 合遝乘夜潛登和尚原絕頂，宋人驚以為神，皆散走，破其眾二千，生獲數十人。

translations.literal: Hedao climbed Heshangyuan's summit by night; the Song thought it divine and scattered. Two thousand of their force were broken; dozens taken alive.
translations.idiomatic: Hedao scaled Heshangyuan's peak by night. Song soldiers took it for sorcery and fled. Two thousand were shattered; dozens captured.

sentences.zh: 南家斬木開道以登西山，再與宋兵遇，皆敗之，遂盡複故地。

translations.literal: Nanjia cut timber to open a path up Western Mountain, met Song troops twice more, defeated them both, and fully recovered the former territory.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjia hewed a path up Western Mountain, twice met and routed Song forces, and restored all lost ground.

sentences.zh: 宋吳曦將馮興、楊雄、李珪以步騎八千人入赤穀，將寇秦州。

translations.literal: Song Wu Xi's generals Feng Xing, Yang Xiong, and Li Gui led eight thousand foot and horse into Chigu to raid Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi's generals Feng Xing, Yang Xiong, and Li Gui marched eight thousand foot and horse into Chigu intending Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 承裕、完顏璘、河州防禦使蒲察秉鉉逆擊，破之。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu, Wan Yan Lin, and Pucha Bingxian of Hezhou met them and broke their force.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu, Wanyan Lin, and Pucha Bingxian of Hezhou intercepted and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 宋步兵趨西山，騎兵走赤穀。

translations.literal: Song infantry pressed toward Western Mountain; cavalry fled toward Chigu.
translations.idiomatic: Song foot soldiers pressed Western Mountain; horsemen fled toward Chigu.

sentences.zh: 承裕分兵躡宋步兵，宋步兵據山搏戰，部將唐括按答海率二百騎馳擊之，甲士蒙葛挺身先入其陣，眾乘之，宋步兵大潰，殺數百人，追者至皁郊城，斬首二千級。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu divided troops to pursue the Song infantry, who held the mountain and fought desperately. The officer Tangkuo Andahai led two hundred horsemen in a charge; the soldier Mengge threw himself first into their ranks and the rest followed. The Song infantry collapsed; several hundred were killed; pursuit reached Zaojiao City and two thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu split his force to harry the infantry, who fought from the heights. Tangkuo Andahai charged with two hundred horse; Mengge plunged in first and the rest followed. The Song foot broke; hundreds fell before pursuit halted at Zaojiao with two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 猛安把添奴追宋騎兵，殺千余人，馮興僅以身免，楊雄、李珪皆為金軍所殺。

translations.literal: The meng'an Batiannu pursued the Song cavalry and killed more than a thousand. Feng Xing barely escaped with his life; Yang Xiong and Li Gui were both slain by Jin troops.
translations.idiomatic: Batiannu chased the cavalry and killed over a thousand. Feng Xing alone escaped; Yang Xiong and Li Gui died to Jin arms.

sentences.zh: 十月，綱以蕃、漢步騎一萬出臨潭，充以關中兵一萬出陳倉，蒲察貞以岐、隴兵一萬出成紀，石抹仲溫以隴右步騎五千出鹽川，完顏璘以本部兵五千出來遠。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Gang led ten thousand Fan and Han foot and horse out of Lintan; Yanzhou led ten thousand Guanzhong troops out through Chencang; Pucha Zhen led ten thousand Qi-Long troops out of Chengji; Shimo Zhongwen led five thousand Longyou foot and horse out of Yanchuan; Wan Yan Lin led five thousand of his own troops out of Laiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Gang marched ten thousand Fan and Han troops from Lintan; Yanzhou ten thousand Guanzhong men through Chencang; Pucha Zhen ten thousand from Qi-Long through Chengji; Shimo Zhongwen five thousand Longyou soldiers through Yanchuan; Wanyan Lin five thousand from Laiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，吳玠、吳璘俱為宋大將，兄弟父子相繼守西土，得梁、益間士眾心。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wu Jie and Wu Lin had both been great Song generals; father, sons, and brothers in succession held the western lands and won the hearts of the gentry and commoners between Liang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie and Wu Lin had been Song's great western commanders; their family held the frontier for generations and won the loyalty of Liang and Yi.

sentences.zh: 璘孫曦太尉、昭武軍節度使、成都潼川府夔利等州路宣撫副使，泰和六年出兵興元，有窺關、隴之志，誘募邊民為盜，遣諜以利餌鳳翔卒溫昌，結三虞候軍為內應。

translations.literal: Lin's grandson Xi was Grand Marshal, military commissioner of Zhaowu, and vice pacification commissioner of the Chengdu-Tongchuan-Fuzhou-Kuizhou-Lizhou circuit. In the sixth year of Taihe he marched from Xingyuan with designs on Tong and Long, incited border people as bandits, and sent spies with profit to bribe the Fengxiang soldier Wen Chang and win the Three Guards as inside accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's grandfather was Wu Lin. Xi held rank as Grand Marshal and vice pacification commissioner of Chengdu and the western circuits. In Taihe's sixth year he advanced from Xingyuan toward Tong and Long, stirred border bandits, and bribed Fengxiang's Wen Chang to turn the Three Guards.

sentences.zh: 昌詣府上變。

translations.literal: Chang came to the prefecture to report the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Chang reported the conspiracy at the prefectural yamen.

sentences.zh: 曦遣諸將出秦、隴間，與綱等諸軍相拒。

translations.literal: Xi sent his generals out between Qin and Long to confront Gang and the other armies.
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent generals into Qin and Long to face Gang's forces.

sentences.zh: 上聞韓侂胄忌曦威名，可以間誘致之，梁、益居宋上游，可以得志于宋，封曦蜀國王，鑄印賜詔，詔綱經略之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Han Tuozhou resented Xi's renown and that he might be lured by discord; Liang and Yi lay upstream of Song and success against Song could be achieved. Xi was enfeoffed King of Shu, a seal cast and an edict bestowed, and Gang was ordered to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The throne learned Han Tuozhou envied Xi's fame and that discord might win him. Liang and Yi dominated Song's upper reaches—here was leverage. Xi was named King of Shu; a seal and edict were sent, and Gang directed the stratagem.

sentences.zh: 其賜曦詔曰：

translations.literal: The edict bestowed on Xi read:
translations.idiomatic: The edict to Xi began:

sentences.zh: 宋自佶、桓失守，構竄江表，僭稱位號，偷生吳會，時則乃祖武安公玠捍禦兩川。

translations.literal: Since Song's Huizong and Qinzong lost the north and fled to skulk south of the Yangzi, usurping a throne and clinging to life in Wu and Yue, your ancestor the Duke of Martial Tranquility Jie then defended the two Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Song's emperors Huizong and Qinzong lost the realm and fled south of the Yangzi, clinging to Wu and Yue. Your ancestor Wu Jie, Duke of Martial Tranquility, then held the two Shu.

sentences.zh: 洎武順王璘嗣有大勳，固宜世胙大帥，遂荒西土，長為籓輔，誓以河山，後裔縱有欒黶之汰，猶當十世宥之。

translations.literal: When the Martial Compliance King Lin inherited his great merit, it was right that his house should enfeoff a grand marshal in perpetuity, long guard the western lands as a border vassal, and swear on river and mountain—even if descendants had faults of extravagance, they should still receive ten generations of pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Lin, Martial Compliance King, inherited that merit, your house rightly held the west as Song's shield, sworn on river and mountain—even descendants' excesses merited ten generations of grace.

sentences.zh: 然威略震主者身危，功蓋天下者不賞，自古如此，非止於今。

translations.literal: Yet one whose might awes his lord endangers his person; one whose merit eclipses the realm goes unrewarded—from antiquity it has been so, not only today.
translations.idiomatic: He whose prowess shadows his sovereign risks his life; he whose merit outshines the realm goes unrewarded. This was ever thus.

sentences.zh: 卿家專制蜀漢，積有歲年，猜嫌既萌，進退維谷，代之而不受，召之而不赴，君臣之義，已同路人，譬之破桐之葉不可以複合，騎虎之勢不可以中下矣。

translations.literal: Your house has monopolized Shu and Han for many years; suspicion has sprouted and advance and retreat are a ravine. To replace you they would not accept it; to summon you you would not come—the bond of sovereign and minister is already that of strangers on the road. Split paulownia leaves cannot be joined again; one who rides a tiger cannot dismount midway.
translations.idiomatic: Your clan ruled Shu-Han for years until suspicion ripened and you stood in a ravine between throne and ruin. Song would not keep you yet would not let you go—sovereign and minister are strangers now. Split paulownia leaves will not rejoin; he who rides a tiger cannot climb down halfway.

sentences.zh: 此事流傳，稔於朕聽，每一思之，未嘗不當饋歎息，而卿猶偃然自安。

translations.literal: This tale has spread and ripened in our hearing; each time We reflect on it We cannot but sigh—and yet you still repose at ease.
translations.idiomatic: We have long heard this tale and sighed each time—yet you still rest at ease.

sentences.zh: 且卿自視翼贊之功孰與岳飛？

translations.literal: Moreover, do you yourself judge—whose supporting merit compares with Yue Fei's?
translations.idiomatic: Tell us: whose merit compares with Yue Fei's?

sentences.zh: 飛之威名戰功暴於南北，一旦見忌，遂被三夷之誅，可不畏哉。

translations.literal: Yue's renown and battle merit thundered north and south; once he was envied he suffered execution to the third degree of kin—should you not fear?
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei's fame shook north and south; envy brought the extermination of three degrees of kin. Will you not fear?

sentences.zh: 故智者順時而動，明者因機而發，與其負高世之勳見疑於人，惴惴然常懼不得保其首領，曷若順時因機，轉禍為福，建萬世不朽之業哉！

translations.literal: Therefore the wise move with the times and the clear seize opportunity. Rather than bear supreme merit of the age and be suspected by others, trembling in constant fear for your head, how much better to follow the times, turn calamity to blessing, and build an enterprise immortal for ten thousand generations!
translations.idiomatic: The wise bend with the hour; the clear seize the moment. Better to turn with fortune than cling to perilous glory and tremble for your head—build an immortal name instead!

sentences.zh: 今趙擴昏孱，受制強臣，比年以來，頓違誓約，增屯軍馬，招納叛亡。

translations.literal: Now Zhao Kuo is dim and feeble, controlled by powerful ministers. In recent years he has repeatedly broken sworn treaties, increased garrison troops, and harbored defectors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuo reigns weakly, ruled by strong ministers. He has broken treaties, massed troops, and sheltered deserters.

sentences.zh: 朕以生靈之故，未欲遽行討伐，姑遣有司移文，複因來使宣諭，而乃不顧道理，愈肆憑陵，虔劉我邊陲，攻剽我城邑。

translations.literal: For the sake of the people We have not wished to launch punishment hastily, but first sent officials with documents; again through the envoy We proclaimed counsel—yet heedless of reason he has grown ever more arrogant, slaughtering Our border people and storming Our walled towns.
translations.idiomatic: For the people's sake We delayed war and sent word—yet Song scorned reason, ravaged Our borders, and stormed Our cities.

sentences.zh: 是以忠臣扼腕，義士痛心，家與為仇，人百其勇，失道至此，雖欲不亡得乎？

translations.literal: Thus loyal ministers clench their fists and righteous men ache in heart; every household treats them as enemies and every man brings a hundredfold courage. Having lost the Way to this point, though they wished not to perish, could they succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Loyal hearts ache; every home counts Song an enemy and every man fights with hundredfold zeal. Having lost the Way, can they not perish?

sentences.zh: 朕已分命虎臣，臨江問罪，長驅並騖，飛渡有期，此正豪傑分功之秋也。

translations.literal: We have already ordered tiger generals to ask guilt at the Yangzi, to drive long and race together—the day of flying crossing is near. This is the season when heroes divide the merit.
translations.idiomatic: Our tiger generals already march on the Yangzi; the day of crossing draws near. This is the hour for heroes to claim their share.

sentences.zh: 卿以英偉之姿，處危疑之地，必能深識天命，洞見事機。

translations.literal: You with heroic stature stand in peril and doubt; you must deeply know Heaven's mandate and clearly see the turn of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: You stand in peril with heroic gifts—you must read Heaven's mandate and seize the moment.

sentences.zh: 若按兵閉境，不為異同，使我師並力巢穴，而無西顧之虞，則全蜀之地，卿所素有，當加封冊，一依皇統冊構故事。

translations.literal: If you hold your troops and close your borders without taking sides, letting Our armies combine strength on the nest and have no worry of looking west, then all the land of Shu that you have long held shall receive enfeoffment according to the precedent of enfeoffing Gou in the Huangtong era.
translations.idiomatic: Hold your borders neutral while Our armies strike Song's heartland without glancing west, and all Shu you hold shall be enfeoffed as Gou was in Huangtong.

sentences.zh: 更能順流東下，助為掎角，則旌麾所指，盡以相付。

translations.literal: If you can further float east with the current and aid as a pincer, then wherever Our banners point all shall be entrusted to you.
translations.idiomatic: If you also strike east in concert, wherever Our banners turn shall be yours.

sentences.zh: 天日在上，朕不食言。

translations.literal: Heaven and sun are above; We do not eat Our words.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and sun witness: We do not break Our word.

sentences.zh: 今送金寶一鈕，至可領也。

translations.literal: Now We send one clasp of gold and jewels—on arrival you may receive them.
translations.idiomatic: We send a clasp of gold and jewels—receive them on arrival.

sentences.zh: 綱次臨江被詔，進至水洛，訪得曦族人端，署為水洛城巡檢使，遣持詔間行諭曦。

translations.literal: Gang, having halted at Linjiang to receive the edict, advanced to Shuiluo, found Xi's clansman Duan, appointed him patrol inspector of Shuiluo City, and sent him with the edict by a hidden route to instruct Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Gang, receiving orders at Linjiang, advanced to Shuiluo, found Xi's kinsman Duan, made him patrol inspector of Shuiluo, and sent him with the edict by secret path to Xi.

sentences.zh: 曦得詔意動，程松尚在興元，未敢發，詐稱杖殺端，以蔽匿其事。

translations.literal: Xi was moved by the edict but Cheng Song was still at Xingyuan and he dared not act; he falsely claimed to have beaten Duan to death with the staff to conceal the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xi wavered at the edict, but Cheng Song remained at Xingyuan and he dared not move. He feigned having Duan clubbed to death to hide the plot.

sentences.zh: 松兵既敗，曦乃遣掌管機宜文字姚圓與端奉表送款。

translations.literal: After Cheng Song's army was defeated Xi sent his staff officer Yao Yuan with Duan to present a submission of allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Song fell, Xi sent Yao Yuan with Duan bearing a letter of surrender.

sentences.zh: 綱遣前京北府錄事張仔會吳曦於興州之置口，曦言歸心朝廷無他，張仔請以告身為報，曦盡出以付之，仍獻階州。

translations.literal: Gang sent the former recorder of the North Capital Zhang Zai to meet Wu Xi at Zhekou in Xingzhou. Xi said his heart turned to the court without other intent; Zhang Zai asked for his commission documents as proof and Xi produced them all, also offering Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gang sent Zhang Zai to meet Xi at Xingzhou's Zhekou. Xi swore loyalty; Zhang Zai demanded his commissions as proof and Xi surrendered them all, yielding Jiezhou as well.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以曦初附，恃中國為援，欲先取襄陽以為蜀漢遮罩，乃詔右副元帥匡先攻襄陽，詔略曰：「陝西一面雖下四州，吳曦之降朕所經略。

translations.literal: The court, because Xi had just submitted and relied on the Central Court as support, wished first to take Xiangyang as a screen for Shu-Han and therefore decreed the Right Vice Marshal Kuang to attack Xiangyang first. The edict in summary said: "Though four prefectures on the Shaanxi front have fallen, Wu Xi's surrender is what We have been directing.
translations.idiomatic: The court, trusting Xi's fresh allegiance, sought Xiangyang first as a shield for Shu-Han and ordered Right Vice Marshal Kuang to strike it. The edict said: "Though Shaanxi lost four prefectures, Xi's surrender is Our doing.

sentences.zh: 自大軍出境，惟卿所部力戰為多，方之前人無所愧謝。

translations.literal: Since the great army crossed the border your division alone has fought hardest; compared with those before you, you have nothing to regret.
translations.idiomatic: Since the armies marched, yours alone fought hardest—no shame beside your forebears.

sentences.zh: 今南伐之事責成卿等，區區俘獲不足羡慕，果能為國建功，豈止一身榮寵，後世子孫，亦保富貴。」

translations.literal: Now the southern campaign is entrusted to you. Petty captives are not worth envy; if you truly build merit for the state, it is not only personal glory and favor—your descendants too shall keep their wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The southern war rests on you. Small spoils matter little; true merit enriches your line for generations."

sentences.zh: 匡得詔，乃移兵趨襄陽。

translations.literal: Kuang received the edict and shifted his army toward Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang took the order and marched on Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，曦遣果州團練使郭澄、仙人關使任辛奉表及蜀地圖志、吳氏譜牒來上。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Xi sent Guo Cheng, regimental commander of Guozhou, and Ren Xin, keeper of Xianren Pass, to present memorials with maps and gazetteers of Shu and the Wu genealogy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xi sent Guo Cheng of Guozhou and Ren Xin of Xianren Pass with memorials, Shu maps, and the Wu genealogy.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，召綱赴京師，以為陝西宣撫副使，進三階。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year Gang was summoned to the capital and made vice pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, advanced three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year's first month Gang was called to court as vice pacification commissioner of Shaanxi and advanced three ranks.

sentences.zh: 還軍，吳曦遣郭澄進謝恩表、誓表、賀全蜀歸附三表，親王百官稱賀，朝廷以詔答之，並賜誓詔。

translations.literal: Returning to the army, Wu Xi sent Guo Cheng with memorials of thanks, oaths, and congratulation on the full submission of Shu; princes and officials offered felicitations; the court answered with an edict and bestowed an oath edict.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the field, Xi sent Guo Cheng with thanks, oaths, and congratulations on Shu's submission. Princes and officials celebrated; the court replied with edict and oath.

sentences.zh: 郭澄朝辭，諭澄曰：「汝主效順，以全蜀歸附，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When Guo Cheng took leave for audience he was instructed: "Your lord has shown loyalty in submitting all Shu. We are greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At Guo Cheng's farewell audience he heard: "Your master has loyally surrendered all Shu. We are well pleased.

sentences.zh: 然立國日淺，恐宋兵侵軼，人心不安，凡有當行事務已委宣撫完顏綱移文計議。

translations.literal: Yet the state is newly founded and Song troops may raid; hearts are not yet at ease. All matters requiring action have been entrusted to Pacification Commissioner Wan Yan Gang by dispatch for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: His realm is young; Song may raid and hearts waver. Wanyan Gang shall handle all affairs by dispatch.

sentences.zh: 或有緊急，即差人就去講究。

translations.literal: If anything is urgent, send men at once to consult on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent matters: send envoys at once for counsel.

sentences.zh: 大定間，汝主嘗以事入覲，今亦多歲，朕嘉汝主之義，懷想不忘，欲得其繪像，如見其面。

translations.literal: In the Dading era your lord once came to court on business; many years have passed. We cherish your lord's righteousness and think of him without forgetting; We wish to have his painted likeness as though seeing his face.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading your master visited court—long ago now. We cherish him and desire his portrait as though we saw his face.

sentences.zh: 今已遣使封冊，俟回日附進。

translations.literal: Envoys for enfeoffment have been sent; when they return the portrait shall be forwarded.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffment envoys are dispatched; the portrait will follow on their return.

sentences.zh: 可以此意歸諭汝主。」

translations.literal: You may convey this intent to your lord on your return.
translations.idiomatic: Bear this message home to your master."

sentences.zh: 詔以同知臨洮府事術虎高琪為封冊使，翰林直學士喬宇副之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shuhu Gaoqi, vice-prefect of Lintao, enfeoffment envoy, with Hanlin Academician Qiao Yu as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Shuhu Gaoqi of Lintao was named enfeoffment envoy; Academician Qiao Yu his deputy.

sentences.zh: 詔高琪曰：「卿以邊面宣力，加之讀書，蜀人識卿威名，勿以財賄動心，失大國體。

translations.literal: The edict to Gaoqi said: "You have exerted yourself on the frontier and moreover read books; the people of Shu know your martial renown. Do not let bribes move your heart and lose the dignity of a great state.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi was told: "You have served the frontier and read books; Shu knows your name. Do not let gifts sway you and shame the realm.

sentences.zh: 檢制隨去奉職，勿有違枉生事。」

translations.literal: Control the attendants who go with you; do not bend the law and create trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Control your retinue; do not abuse authority."

sentences.zh: 頃之，宋安丙殺吳曦。

translations.literal: Before long Song An Bing killed Wu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon An Bing of Song slew Wu Xi.

sentences.zh: 上聞曦死，遣使責綱，詔曰：「曦之降，自當進據仙人關，以制蜀命，且為曦重。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard Xi was dead he sent envoys to rebuke Gang. The edict said: "When Xi submitted you should at once have advanced to hold Xianren Pass to control Shu's fate and thereby add weight to Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Xi's death, the throne rebuked Gang: "On his surrender you should have seized Xianren Pass to hold Shu and strengthen him.

sentences.zh: 既不據關，複撤兵，使丙無所憚，是宜有今日也。」

translations.literal: Having neither held the pass nor withdrawn troops, you let Bing act without fear—today's outcome was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: You held no pass and withdrew troops, leaving Bing unafraid—today was inevitable."

sentences.zh: 於是，詔贈曦太師，命德順州刺史完顏思忠招魂葬于水洛縣。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict posthumously enfeoffed Xi Grand Preceptor and ordered Dezun prefect Wan Yan Sizhong to summon his soul and bury him at Shuiluo County.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was posthumously made Grand Preceptor; Wanyan Sizhong of Dezun was ordered to conduct his soul and bury him at Shuiluo.

sentences.zh: 以曦族兄端之子為曦後。

translations.literal: Xi's clansman Duan's son was made heir to Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Duan's son, Xi's kinsman, was appointed his heir.

sentences.zh: 詔諭陝西軍士，略曰：「汝等爰自去冬，出疆用命，擐披甲胄，冒涉艱險，直取山外數州，比之他軍實有勤效。

translations.literal: An edict instructed the Shaanxi soldiers, in summary: "You from last winter onward have crossed the borders and expended your lives, donned armor, braved hardships and dangers, and directly seized several prefectures beyond the mountains—in comparison with other armies you have truly shown meritorious effort.
translations.idiomatic: An edict addressed the Shaanxi soldiers, in summary: "Since last winter you have crossed the borders at the cost of your lives, donned armor, braved hardship, and seized several prefectures beyond the mountains. Compared with other armies, your merit is real.

sentences.zh: 界外屯駐日久，負勞苦，恩賞未行，有司申奏不明，以致如此。

translations.literal: Garrisoned beyond the borders for a long time, you bear hardships; favors and rewards have not been granted; the responsible offices reported unclearly, leading to this situation.
translations.idiomatic: You have garrisoned beyond the borders for a long time and borne hardship, yet rewards have not been granted because the responsible offices reported unclearly—hence this situation.

sentences.zh: 朕已令增給賞物，以酬爾勞。

translations.literal: I have already ordered additional rewards to requite your labors.
translations.idiomatic: I have ordered additional rewards to repay your labor.

sentences.zh: 惟是餘賊未殄，猶須經略。

translations.literal: Only the remaining bandits are not yet exterminated and still require planning and control.
translations.idiomatic: Only the remaining enemy is not yet destroyed and still requires our attention.

sentences.zh: 眷我師徒，久役未解，深懷憫念，寤寐弗忘。

translations.literal: Cherishing my armies, long in service without release, I deeply harbor compassion and forget it neither waking nor sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: I cherish my armies, long in service without release, and think of you with compassion waking and sleeping.

sentences.zh: 汝等益思體國之忠，奮敵愾之勇，協心畢力，建立功勳；

translations.literal: You should further consider loyalty to the state, rouse the courage of hatred for the enemy, unite your hearts and exhaust your strength, and establish achievements;
translations.idiomatic: Think further on loyalty to the state, rouse your courage against the enemy, unite your hearts and give your full strength to win merit;

sentences.zh: 高爵厚祿，朕所不吝。」

translations.literal: high rank and thick emoluments—I do not begrudge them."
translations.idiomatic: high rank and generous rewards—I withhold none."

sentences.zh: 宋人複陷階州、西和州，綱至鳳翔，詔徹五州之兵退保要害，五州之民願徙內地者厚撫集之。

translations.literal: The Song again captured Jiezhou and Xihezhou; Gang reached Fengxiang; an edict ordered the armies of the five prefectures withdrawn to guard key points; the people of the five prefectures who wished to move inland were generously comforted and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: The Song again captured Jiezhou and Xihezhou. Gang reached Fengxiang. An edict ordered troops withdrawn from the five prefectures to hold key points, and people who wished to move inland were generously resettled.

sentences.zh: 以近侍局直長為四川安慰使。

translations.literal: A director of the Inner Attendants Bureau was made Sichuan consolation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A director of the Inner Attendants Bureau was appointed Sichuan consolation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蒲察貞撤黃牛戍，宋安丙乘之，連兵來襲，遂陷散關，鞏州鈐轄兀顏阿失死之。

translations.literal: Pucha Zhen withdrew the Huangniu garrison; the Song An Bing seized the opportunity, brought troops in succession to attack, and thus captured Sanshui Pass; the Gongzhou commander Wanyan Ashi died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Zhen withdrew the Huangniu garrison. Song general An Bing seized the chance, attacked in force, and captured Sanshui Pass. Gongzhou commander Wanyan Ashi was killed.

sentences.zh: 詔奪綱官一階，降兵部侍郎，權宣撫副使。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Gang of one rank, demoted him to Vice Minister of War, and made him acting Pacification Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Gang of one rank, demoted him to Vice Minister of War, and made him acting Pacification Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遣戶部侍郎尼龐古懷忠按治綱以下將吏。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister of Revenue Nipanggu Huaizhong was dispatched to investigate and punish Gang and the generals and officials below him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Nipanggu Huaizhong was dispatched to investigate Gang and the officers under him.

sentences.zh: 懷忠未至陝西，綱、貞遣兵潛自昆谷西山養馬澗入，四面攻之，複取散關，斬宋將張統領、於團練。

translations.literal: Before Huaizhong reached Shaanxi, Gang and Zhen secretly sent troops in from Yangmadong on the western mountain of Kungu Valley, attacked from four sides, recaptured Sanshui Pass, and beheaded the Song generals Commander Zhang and Regiment Commander Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Before Huaizhong reached Shaanxi, Gang and Zhen secretly sent troops through Yangmadong on Kungu Valley's western slope, attacked from four sides, recaptured Sanshui Pass, and beheaded Song commanders Zhang and Yu.

sentences.zh: 綱遣使奏捷，詔書獎諭，貞等釋不問。

translations.literal: Gang sent envoys to report victory; an edict praised and instructed him; Zhen and others were released without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Gang reported victory by envoy. An edict praised him, and Zhen and others were released without punishment.

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎斬關入中都，遷衛紹王于衛邸，命綱子安和作家書，使親信人召綱。

translations.literal: Hushahu cut through the pass and entered Zhongdu, moved Prince Wei Shao to the Wei residence, ordered Gang's son Anhe to write a family letter, and sent a trusted man to summon Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Hushahu forced the pass and entered Zhongdu, moved Prince Wei Shao to the Wei residence, had Gang's son Anhe write a family letter, and sent a trusted man to summon Gang.

sentences.zh: 綱至，囚之憫忠寺，明日，押至市中，使張霖卿數以失四川、敗縉山之事，殺之。

translations.literal: When Gang arrived he was imprisoned at Minzhong Temple; the next day he was escorted to the market; Zhang Linqing enumerated his loss of Sichuan and defeat at Jinshan, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gang arrived he was imprisoned at Minzhong Temple. The next day he was led to the market, where Zhang Linqing recounted his loss of Sichuan and defeat at Jinshan, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 弟 定奴

translations.literal: Younger brother: Dingnu
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Dingnu

sentences.zh: 贊曰：章宗伐宋之役，三易主帥，兵家所忌也。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: In Zhangzong's campaign against Song, the supreme commander was changed three times—what military strategists most dread.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: In Zhangzong's campaign against Song the supreme commander was changed three times—the very thing strategists dread.

sentences.zh: 宋不知乘此以為功，猶曰有人焉？

translations.literal: Song did not know how to seize this to achieve merit—can they still say they have capable men?
translations.idiomatic: Song did not know how to turn this to their advantage—can they still claim capable men?

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄心強智疏，蘇師旦謀淺任大，函首燕、薊，南北皆曰賊臣，何哉？

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou was strong in heart but shallow in wisdom; Su Shidan's scheming was shallow yet his responsibility great; their heads in boxes reached Yan and Ji—north and south all called them traitor ministers. How could it be?
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou was bold but shallow; Su Shidan schemed lightly yet bore great responsibility. Their heads in boxes reached Yan and Ji, and north and south alike called them traitor ministers. How could it be otherwise?

sentences.zh: 完顏匡、完顏綱皆泰和終功之臣，然匡隳忠於大安，綱罔難於至甯，富貴之惑人，乃如此邪？

translations.literal: Wan Yan Kuang and Wan Yan Gang were both ministers who completed the achievements at the end of Taihe, yet Kuang destroyed his loyalty in Da'an and Gang obscured difficulty in Zhiyong—can the bewilderment wrought by wealth and rank be thus indeed?
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Kuang and Wanyan Gang both crowned the Taihe achievements, yet Kuang betrayed his loyalty in Da'an and Gang evaded blame in Zhiyong—is this how wealth and rank bewilder men?
